# Character State — After Chapter 48 (VOLUME 01 CLOSE)

## Jonas Mercer

- **Age / role:** 32; NDC field technician, **grade III, probationary, and expecting nothing else.** He was granted the appointment on 27 March and it was declined in writing on 29 March. As of 20 April he holds **no appointment, no cabinet (6-R-14 drawer four closed), and no gate-initiation rights at 6-41.**
- **Public title, 19 April:** entered on a **REGISTER OF ATTACHMENT** as **LAST WORKING SYSTEM ADMINISTRATOR, CITY OF NACRE.** Civic standing, not departmental. No grade, no probation, not subject to review. **Released by no person.** He was in the gallery of a committee as a witness to a contractor's determination, was not asked, asked one question — *can it be taken off* — and was told no. **Oren Pell stated the reason in the room and had it minuted: the register gives him no root access, no precedence, no office, no staff, no vote, no key and no right to refuse an attachment, and it puts his name where the city can find it so that claims land in the open instead of in a series 6 drawer. *It is a bucket under a tap, and the tap is going to run for a long time.*** Fenella Marsh refused to minute the title until the basis was stated.
- **Power:** Stage 2, unchanged. In Chapter 46 he performed his **third bounded civic edit** — the Saint Orra bridge **west-lane hinge**, one field, precedence only, at a plate he does not own, **instructed by the dispatcher whose name is in the issuer field**, with the unpaid maintenance claim belonging to that holder, witnessed by Nora Bell, with a second bearer, and **two handovers in the log in fifty minutes.** The obsolete empty-crossing clause behind it is untouched and is named by Dev Singh as the next fight. He still cannot renew a term he did not issue, read the root, write a root clause, issue a citywide command, or make anybody consent.
- **Body:** the seam mark runs past the elbow into the upper arm. The right hand is numb to the elbow and will not close. He braces a roofing slate under a cover and holds it with his forearm for the whole of a mend.
- **Claims against him:** the west-clinic care-entrance maintenance claim, assigned by default in the series 6 file; the 6-L/14 chamber-and-bank unclaimed burden went to **Royden Achebe** on 18 April; and now **every future unclaimed burden on the lowland chain is routed to him first, by a register, in public.** Oren Pell said that a person would have been better and that the person would have been a resident of a street with no address, and named no names, and was stopped from naming them by a councillor in a public room.
- **Public record:** issuer line on a live plate at the hospital door, which Marta Sowle asked to come off the public board and which is not the public board and which a plate has no field to remove; a refused waiver on the Old Ward board; six words he wrote; a condition line he declined to read into a minute and which a registrar has now read into a record; a term on the west-lane hinge at a bridge; a job card in his coat with eight names, five refusals and a key.
- **Flaw in action, named by six people:** he reaches for competence instead of asking. This batch he asked a doctor in a corridor in front of two people and got a no, and a woman of sixty-one in a kitchen and got a no, and he wrote both refusals down in full and went away with eight names instead of nine.
- **Change in this batch:** he asked. That is the whole of it, and it cost him the ninth line twice and the second line once, and he has learned that the cost of asking is not the same as the cost of not asking, and that he has been paying the second one for five weeks and did not know it.

## Dr. Sanaa Iqbal

- **Age / role:** 35; Saint Orra emergency physician. Named on-call clinician in the gate's fallback clause.
- **The ninth line, 7 April:** **refused**, in a corridor, in front of Mina Okafor and Ruth Nwosu, and gave a reason he had not prepared her with — a doctor who both declares emergencies and certifies the term that authorises them is a conflict of interest on the face of a document, and the first thing anybody in June will read is that.
- **And then she told him the thing she had been carrying:** since 24 March she has been trying to get a **second named clinician** on the west-clinic roster. Four refusals from consultants and one outright no from the education office, because a second on-call is a rota line and a rota line is money, and the money came off the department when the participation fund withdrew. **She had not told him because he would have made it a thing about a card.** And it was.
- **Action on 18 April:** called at 03:12, in a shirt, and gave a declaration in nine seconds. Not a rescue and not a reconciliation. **She is not on the card and did not say yes and did not say almost yes.**
- **Current view of Jonas:** the man who finally asked, in a corridor, where it could be written down, and got a better answer than the one he had prepared, and did not argue with it.
- **Trust state:** not certified, and not asking to be. **The design is not the problem is a shop steward's sentence in a public document and she is not the author of it and has not been asked to endorse it.**

## Tomas Renn

- **Age / role:** 44; Civic Continuity Workers' Union shop steward, former NDC field supervisor.
- **The fourth question:** asked five times, and **worked at a sixth time on 15 April** when two people on one rota refused and the least-bad option was a night orderly with a laundry bag. **He then put the answer in a document.**
- **The submission, filed 09:14 on Friday 18 April**, four days early, in the public papers for the June folder, with a minority report because Ada Kwarteng and Cuthbert Nkemelu would not sign. **The finding: *the civic term architecture was not the failure on the third of April and was not the failure on the fifteenth, and the record should not be permitted to suggest otherwise.*** It is in his name alone.
- **The cost, which he named first:** a demand became a finding, a finding can only be cited, and it will be cited first by a continuity contractor, because it is the only sentence in the world that says nothing in the design caused this. **He is no longer the only person asking in the city and he did it on purpose, and he told nobody at the shop.**
- **His own counter-finding, in a yard and not in the document:** the architecture **was** the problem. On the third, the term was live and the door shut at six because **a renewal clause requires two people to be in a corridor at ten at night and cannot require anybody to be there.** That is not luck. That is a rule that puts a rota in charge of a promise. **He has three of four prerequisites and the third is a hospital doctor's good intentions, and he says he is fifty per cent of the problem now instead of sixty, and the question is not answered, and Jonas does not answer it.**
- **He refused a CivicCore joint working paper in a sentence.** Jonas heard about it on the Saturday from Bea Osunde and did not go and find him.

## Nell Ardent

- **Age / role:** 39; founder of the Open Covenants Legal Clinic.
- **Role in this batch:** acting for the Cooper's Reach residents' association and **not for the city**, at the 23 April panel, for nothing, once, at £95 an hour thereafter. **Slept two of five nights in the Methodist hall on Carrow Lane with eleven Brine Wharf households who have been paying for nothing since 13 April**, and refused a joint working paper of her own that a contractor had produced on the night of the surge, and told Jonas in a corridor what the only useful thing anybody had said to her that week was: *the count is not free. Everyone thinks the count is the paperwork. The count is the day somebody comes with a clipboard and asks a person to be on a piece of paper, and after that the person is on it forever, and there is no unlisting anybody.*
- **Boundary:** not neutral, not a rescue. She told a Methodist hall the appeal will probably fail and filed it anyway.

## Pia Santos

- **Age / role:** 19; bicycle courier, caregiver, and route representative.
- **Action in this batch:** refused him **again**, on 7 April, in four lines written on a step in the rain, and required that it be written **once** so that a hearing could not say there were two people on the seventh line. **Her refusal stands.** She said the seventh line is hers if it is anybody's and that she is not going to be it.
- **The 18 April scene:** she told a councillor of the Civic Assembly that the answer to *who is the other end of it* is the other end of it, and that the councillor was the first person in thirty-two years to come up the path and say that out loud, and that she was not being kind about it and was also not going to pretend it was nothing.
- **Boundary:** unchanged. Not a spokesperson, not a signature, not on the Weir's rota, not on the card. **She asked the Weir's question and got an answer from an institution and gave it back to the residents without editing it.**

## Oren Pell

- **Age / role:** deputy registrar enforcing public-safety and emergency-service terms.
- **Action in this batch:** refused a determination in a car on the Salt Row embankment at 02:20 on 18 April, and entered **two findings in one record, in one hand, in the same minute** — that a term which ends on its own terms has not failed, and that **a contractor's contractual definition of failure is not a civic determination of a node's state**, and he also entered that the door would have been shut at ten past three and a woman of ninety-one moved in a flooding corridor on a doctor's own signature, which is worse than anything in the agreement. **He said he has run out of ways of not giving the other side a witness.**
- **The 6-L/14 condition line** is now in a registrar's record, entered by him, at about seven in the evening on 18 April, with Jonas present, and the record says for the file — and not for Jonas — **that the line was available to be recorded on 1 April and was not.**
- **The register of attachment is his instrument and he said so in a room and had it minuted.** He tried to describe the three residents an unclaimed burden would otherwise have gone to, and **Councillor Sore stopped him, and he complied, and the minute was corrected.**
- **Standing position:** the man who will read the next thing and put his name on it, and who has never once been thanked. **He is on Jonas's side of the argument and against his own department and against the city's convenience, and he has said what that costs.**

## Royden Achebe

- **Age / role:** 49; NDC field services manager. **Holder of the interim lowland maintenance post in his own name**, taken on 1 April within seconds of Jonas refusing it, having withdrawn a draft on 14 March for the opposite reason.
- **Action in this batch:** **accepted an unclaimed burden by telephone from a yard in Gantry Ward at about seven in the evening on 18 April, in nine words, and said he would rather have had it before he had the post.** The burden is 6-L/14: the chamber and the bank, with four tonnes of stone owed, a flap, and a man who wrote his own classification on it. **A report is due 29 May.**
- **In the committee room on 19 April he gave the date, said it will require somebody to know where the node is, said the honest answer from that table is that nobody does, and said that the seventeenth of April made his problem bigger and gave it a name, which is what a public record is for.**
- **Current position:** he is the answer on a file of his own authorship and now on a second, and he is worse than Jonas, and he has said the sentence that makes it visible without explaining it, and **nobody in the building can minute it.**

## Nina Calder

- **Age / role:** NDC records supervisor, she/her. Countersigned the responsibility bond as records.
- **Action in this batch:** drafted the register of attachment **twice**, was told to draft it twice, read it out in a committee room, and invented the phrase **released by no person** — which she did to keep an unclaimed burden off a resident, which is the register of a records clerk inventing a legal protection for a street she has never been to.
- **Position:** she has minuted a refusal of a contract, the words of nine people, a woman's reason for not wanting a clause, a woman of ninety-one's numbers, a registrar's two findings, and a contractor's definition of failure — and has not once been asked which side she is on.

## Dr. Sethi

- **Role:** Saint Orra day-team physician and the clinic's naming authority. **Line nine on the card, as a west clinic and not as a hospital.**
- **Condition of consent, in his own words, on the record:** he named Bram Osei, Ezra Mbeki and Ruth Nwosu on the rota in the first week of March on his own signature; two of them have refused shifts since; **if his name goes on a card with a subject on it, the first question anybody asks in June is whether the hospital's witness is the man who named the porters, and the answer is yes, and he will say yes in a room before anybody finds out.** He will not witness a hospital: *there is no such thing as a hospital, there are forty of them, and the day a card says a hospital in a room in June it will mean the one the man in the coat wanted.*
- **Action on 18 April:** called at 03:12, in a shirt, and was the witness at the handover that made the care entrance work on the night of the surge. On 17 April he spent forty minutes in a yard in the rain saying almost nothing.

## Mina Okafor

- **Role:** west-clinic transfer clerk.
- **Action in this batch:** **withdrew from the card at 15:35 on Wednesday 9 April, in her own hand, with the reason written underneath** — *three conditions were set on 2 April. The third was a date. There is no cheque.* She said she was not angry, and asked for that to be in whatever was written about it, and said that a card with a subject on it is a list.

Those are two facts and she said so first.** On 15 April Marta Sowle set the box's counting rule out loud before the number existed — *the box counts what a family was left not knowing, and it does not count how long a door took* — Mina Okafor wrote the rule in first, **declined to enter a figure she had not watched happen**, and then put *forty minutes* in under it, crediting the rule to Marta Sowle in the box; she read the five lines back at the 22:00 handover on Sunday 20 April **because it is her job and because she said so twice to two different people**; she wrote the retainer crossing-out in the box in eleven words' worth of silence; and she put the good line in the box on 18 April — *care entrance open on a live term, two holders, one witness, five lines read aloud, no declaration required, no delay* — and then said, at the same table, that it will be quoted in June next to the forty minutes of Wednesday and the nineteen of Thursday as proof it was handled, and that it is false.

## The witness card — finished, in his coat, not a file

**Eight names, five refusals in full, and line six is a key with no holder.**

1. **A crossing — NORA BELL.** Barrier end and the gate she latches. Refused a council flood forum seat, an annual allowance and a badge, **twice**. Refused to say who crosses it. Relieved of her crossing for the night of 18 April by rail control and did not go back on it.
2. **A door — BRAM OSEI.** Wants his refused Thursday left exactly where it is.
3. **A market — BISI ALADE, 41, fish, five years.** Condition in her own words, said twice: the mended hatch cost her a Saturday and the record must say so. **On 18 April she made the pump operator reverse his decision from fifty feet of cold-store water.** *I am not being a spokesperson for eleven traders. Eleven traders do not need one.*
4. **A pump — EMEKA RUSK.** Held the storm overflow for an hour and ten minutes to keep the market dry, and turned it over when she told him to, alone, at fifty-one, and told nobody until the Monday. The operator box on the fault report is blank and he has decided that is the correct outcome.
5. **A machine — TEO VLAH.** *Machines only*, said first and loudest, every time.
6. **A school — A KEY AND NO HOLDER.** **ROZ IDRIS REFUSED IN THE YARD.** Ibrahim Sesay, 51, took it as a key and opened the school on his own authority at twenty past two in the morning and was shut down by a teacher who is not on the card. **There is no line for what happens to the man who does that, and he said so in the yard.**
7. **A street — YOLANDA FOFANA, 54, Wren Court, Salter's Yard.** Thirty-one rooms, no civic address, a participation fee, and a clause nine. **Jonas said out loud in the yard, at her insistence, that she is not the answer to the Weir.** Three conditions, including that **the fee does not stop**, because the day the fee stops is the day somebody does not get water.
8. **A platform — KOFI SARR.** A platform and never a passenger. Refused a council flood forum dinner on 2 May. **Closed bay four on 18 April and was right, and it cost a lowland its only wheeled exit.**
9. **A west clinic — DR. SETHI.** Will not witness a hospital. Required the record to say he named the porters and has not asked them.

**Refused, in writing, in full, in the lines they belong in: Fola Adeyemi (market, four reasons, her own words). The Weir (street, four lines, read back and not altered — refused by Aurrie Nkemdirim, and refused separately and separately by Pia Santos so that it stays one refusal and not two). Dr. Sanaa Iqbal (hospital, in a corridor, for a reason he had not prepared her with). Mina Okafor (door, withdrawn 9 April, there is no cheque). Roz Idris (school, in the yard, in full).**

**Refused and not on the card at all: Bea Osunde**, in front of everybody, because she works for him. **Tomas Renn**, in a doorway, for eleven minutes, because the shop is not a party. **Fola Adeyemi still holds the collectors' self-collect term by rule eleven and still has the brass tag in her apron pocket, and neither fact softens the other.**

## The Weir residents

- **Aurrie Nkemdirim, sixty-one:** refused line seven in four lines and made him read them back unaltered, and said that a name on a list is a place to send a letter. Read the loft's paper to the west site board on 9 April **sitting down throughout**. **At 16:40 on 17 April she issued a term out loud, standing, in about four minutes, in her own kitchen, for a door, a stove, a floor and Marigold Adjei, seventy-seven, with a chest at the top of the stairs** — said in front of the room that it was not a service and did nothing for Marigold, put the duty on herself because she was the only person there not there because of the forecast, **refused to give her name to a plate, and did not write it down.** It ran thirteen hours and twenty minutes and is the reason there is a shape on a map. **Let a councillor of the Civic Assembly up the towpath on 18 April, on her own terms, and was not asked twice, and said thank you once and meant it.**
- **Marigold Adjei, seventy-seven:** the room at the top of the net-loft stairs, with a chest, unable to manage the stairs twice a day. **Named for the first and only time in the 16:40 term of 17 April and given no name on any plate.** She is not the woman of eighty-four who died in bay six on 15 April and the two must never be conflated. She is a person the volume needed and did not otherwise have time for; Volume 02 may not treat her as a symbol.
- **Margo Doré, sixty-three:** told Jonas on 15 April that if he cleared that trap himself he would stop being a technician who comes to help a street and become a claim, and that a claim is a thing that does not come. **Renewed the stand term on 19 April for one window over a claim she said out loud was false**, and refused a man with a lamp, and stated the price of not having a list before anybody asked her.
- **Ottoline "Otie" Beck, seventy-one:** still holds the tin. Unmentioned in this batch, which is the correct treatment.
- **Bo Trimble, seventeen:** is findable, was already findable, and nothing was added to him. **On 19 April he read a term out loud whose claim he had said was not true, and then read it anyway, and said why on the step in daylight.** He still refuses to carry letters up a path.
- **Hector Mbatha, seventy:** on no line and **not in Chapters 41–48.** His pencil map is still on the Old Ward board frame. The number is still refused and it is still refused without explanation.
- **Wesley Kpomah, forty-four:** refused his Wednesday slot in writing again. Not asked, not present, not added to.
- **Perdita Sow, forty-four:** **in the water for four minutes on 18 April and alive.** Cut thigh, sprained wrist, dislocated finger, at Saint Orra east. The dislocated finger is the one she will be angry about for eleven weeks. **A boy of nineteen on a towpath with a bicycle got her out and nobody has asked his name.** **She is a live thread, not a convenience of the climax: she returns after an absence of sixteen chapters, having been named in 26, 27 and 28 and Ch 45 re-grounds her, and she must be carried forward as a person with an injury and eleven unpaid years of Sundays on that road — not as a body on a bank.** The pencil ring in the loft still reads **THE 22ND, AT 03:00, ON A BANK, NO NAME.**
- **Delphine Ofori, seventy-eight:** not in Chapters 41–48. Her reading of the term to Bo on 5 April is what made the Saturday workable.
- **Ferdy Oduya, thirty-four**, holds the second refuge-store key at Brine Wharf, works nights. **The refuge store was not reached on 17 April and the two thousand four hundred sandbags are in a lock-up behind a key on a seven-to-seven clock.** He is not a Weir resident, is not on the Weir's rota, and was not asked.

## Evan Mercer and Nadia Mercer

- **Evan:** absent. Two cold-chiselled letters, a paint line under an eleven-year-old district ironworks seal, a brass tag in an apron pocket, and a condition line that is now in a registrar's record. **The registrar said in a car park that he was not going to connect them and neither was anybody else in that car park.** None of it is a father.
- **Nadia:** off-page in this batch.

## Relationship Policy

One slow-burn relationship only: Jonas and Sanaa. Volume 01 produced a refusal in a corridor, in front of two people, given for a better reason than he had prepared her with; a piece of professional information she had been carrying since 24 March and had not told him; a declaration at nine seconds; and nothing else. No romance has begun and none may begin before Volume 8.

# Character State — After Chapter 59 (VOLUME 02, BATCH 0001)

## Jonas Mercer

- **Age / role:** 32; NDC field technician, grade III, probationary, no appointment, no cabinet, no gate-initiation rights at 6-41. **On the register of attachment as LAST WORKING SYSTEM ADMINISTRATOR, CITY OF NACRE — civic standing, released by no person.** Not a promotion; it gives no power and no right to refuse an attachment.
- **Power:** Stage 2, unchanged. **Three bounded civic edits in five weeks, all at hinges he does not own, none issued by him.** In Chapter 58 he established a new limit on the page: a stage-2 mending needs a person with local standing to instruct it and a named holder to take it; **a restoration route for a burst pipe is a price, the price is a term, the holder field on that term is the name of a company, and a company cannot be argued with, does not get tired, and is not standing in a chamber at half past twelve in the morning.** He still cannot read the root, write a root clause, issue a citywide command, or make anybody consent.
- **Body:** the seam mark runs past the elbow into the upper arm. The right hand is numb to the elbow and will not close. He braces a roofing slate under a cover and holds it with his forearm for the whole of a mend.
- **What he did in this batch:** refused a money question and named who should answer it; wrote his own failure on a pad and read it out loud; **did not ask Marguerite Oyelaran for anything**; did not read a stranger's card in the claims box; went into a chamber in the dark at half past twelve at night and did not read anything into a public record.
- **Flaw in action, named by six people this batch:** he reaches for competence instead of asking. **Bea Osunde: *you do not get to be modest on behalf of a mortuary gate. That is not restraint. That is a vacuum with your face in it.*** **Perdita Sow: *on Monday I could not tell you which of the two of us you are.*** **Margo Doré: *say that again in a fortnight in a room where it matters.*** **Ivo Bamba, who was right: *I have not got the people who do not come in a van.***
- **Change:** he has learned that **the asking is not the hard part and the being is.** He spent nine days going into rooms, was refused twice, both times correctly, and came away with a number in a woman's handwriting that he then declined to spend. He was told to stay out of a room on 19 May and he said yes.

## Dr. Sanaa Iqbal

- **Age / role:** 35; Saint Orra emergency physician. Named on-call clinician in the gate's fallback clause. **The ninth line is still refused and the refusal stands.**
- **The second named clinician exists.** **Priya Ranganathan, 41**, on the west roster as a named on-call clinician from **2 May**, part-time, on the same terms as her. Found by **Gunnar Halvorsen in about nine hundred pounds of a dead 2011 participation line item**, under a site-administration order on 22 April that did not need a board because it is under four thousand pounds. The fifth refusal reversed for money.
- **The fix and the disease are the same money.** She said it herself: *from where I am standing they are the same word, and the hospital line is nine hundred pounds from 2011 and the block is two pounds sixty a week off thirty-one people, and if those are the same then the whole of what I have said to you in five weeks about care is a thing about money, and it is not, and I would like us to be careful.*
- **The four refusals, given for work and not for trust:** a consultant on 26 March (a rota line is money, I have a person); a consultant on 2 April (I will not be on a rota I did not staff); **the education office on 9 April, which was the no, and the whole letter was *the post is not vacant***; a consultant on 17 April (*not from you*, because he would rather not be a fact in a story the site administration is telling about how it solved a rota).
- **What she told Jonas:** do not prepare anything for me; do not come into a room in June with something I have said in a corridor in April in your pocket. **And that the moment there are two clinicians on the roster the argument in his own head is going to sound like duty, and it is not duty, it is the third of April with a rota and a hole in it.**
- **State:** not reconciled, not closed, not thanked. He asked whether it was all right or the fourth kind, and she told him it was the fourth kind, and he then put the pad on the sill and let her read the mortuary gate.

## Oren Pell

- **Age / role:** 61; deputy registrar, nineteen years in post.
- **Refused to strike a hollow term**, in about ninety seconds, on a telephone, on a Thursday morning, and gave the reason: *a hollow term is a permission that functions. Striking it empties the field. An empty field means the node's maintenance. And the maintenance on a mortuary gate is a man with a key.*
- **And then said the thing nobody has said in this city:** *I have struck four hollow terms in nineteen years and there are about nine hundred of them because we do not count, and every one of them is a sentence somebody wrote in nine seconds for the best reason available to them at the time. I have never seen one before that was in a hospital. This is not a defect of maintenance. It is a defect of the design.*
- **Told Jonas he may not attend the 30 April pre-sitting** — a closed meeting, no gallery, no public box, no public minute, no standing for a man who is not a member, not a party and not a departmental officer — and that he may be at the back of the 19 May hearing if he can stand being at the back of it.
- **Ruled out naming the lowland water point in the porch** of the Old Ward board, on filing grounds, in about forty seconds: describing it would require a location of record; a location of record would be a survey; a survey is a count; a count is the price.
- **Standing position:** on Jonas's side of the argument, against his own department, and he said in the same week that he has been unable to argue with a line a borough panel wrote about water and has been in the job nineteen years.

## Nina Calder

- **Age / role:** NDC records supervisor, she/her. Drafted the register of attachment twice and invented *released by no person*.
- **In this batch she built the first instrument of public revision in this city and told Jonas it was nobody's idea.** The **Return of a Deferred Node**, ten fields, nine lines, a blank rule at the bottom, printed at 2 p.m. on 30 April by a records clerk who had never printed one. Not adopted, not minuted, not enforceable. **She sent Doina Serkis back to the plate to take Ivo Bamba's name out of the first return, because the form is not the place to make a man findable at a gate.**
- **The blank line is not a design feature.** She put it there so the shape of the hole is in the document before somebody prints it on a district with a name. *A form with a hole in it is the only honest thing available to me this week, and I have been a records supervisor for nineteen years and I have never issued one.*
- **Where she got it:** the man at the basement printer, unasked, who said the drawing layer will draw a shape and a term and a date and the claim under it **and has never once drawn what a thing stopped doing.** So the Lattice cannot publish a narrowing and the city can.
- **Told Jonas, unprompted, to say thank you to her from Oren Pell and not to put it in a file.**

## Nell Ardent

- **Age / role:** 39; founder of the Open Covenants Legal Clinic.
- **Found the mechanism of the volume** — clause 4(c) of a participation agreement — in a document she had carried since 2 April, and then refused to make it easier: *those people were not deceived, not coerced, and there was no man in a good coat in that room. I have been doing this for eleven years and I have spent eleven years getting people to sign things, and I have never once been able to make one of them un-sign anything, and this morning I read a piece of paper that says the city has finally built the un-signing button, and it is the shape of a calendar, and there is no appeal against a date.*
- **Told the residents the fee went up. Did not tell them what the up is**, and said so to Jonas, and went to find out whether they have been told.
- **Boundary unchanged:** she told them the appeal would fail and filed it anyway; she is not the city's lawyer; she does not reduce a case to a binary and call it a win.

## Marguerite Oyelaran

- **Age / role:** 47; chief officer of the Carrow Lane Housing Association, two rooms above a betting shop on Carrow Lane, eleven years in post, no assistant. The sign says ASK FOR MARGUERITE.
- **Four blocks, 128 rooms.** Bought Tier 2 on **11 March 2014** for **£16,800**, having read to page two in eleven minutes without knowing she was doing anything anybody could object to. Passed it on at **£2.60 a room a week** off the rent roll, **by putting a standing order form through 128 letterboxes herself on Saturdays in January and February and knocking on every door.** *(The £11 → £13.60 rise is Wren Court's, Salter's Yard, and belongs to Yolanda Fofana. The two may not be run together.)*
- **Why:** the lift in Block D went out for nine days in 2011 and six days in 2004; a man of eighty-three on four went into a care home for eleven weeks and came out of it having lost the use of one side; a board said no to her in a room with nine people in it in ninety seconds because a lift is a piece of plant and no claim attaches to a piece of plant.
- **Her line, and it is the volume's thesis from the wrong end:** *I did not invent the price. I passed it on because I had nowhere to put it.*
- **Said yes in four seconds to putting her own name in six lowland holder fields, and then declined**, and said so out loud, and asked him to write it down: *a person who says yes in four seconds to a thing they know is wrong is worse than a person who says no, and I have done it once in my life and I have just done it in front of you for no reason except that you asked me to wait.*
- **The refusal:** a plate will not take a bare role; an officer findable at six water points on a street with no address is a document with a name on it, and the street will be on the form. **The draw ends. The job does not.**
- **Her own participation counts, and they are hers:** **one hundred and twenty-two of a hundred and twenty-eight signed.** Eight did not; five of the eight said the same sentence, *I will not sign a thing that makes my name a door*; three did not understand it, two of those have since signed and one has not, and she will not ring him a fourth time. **Nine of the hundred and twenty-eight have missed a month.** The page she pushed across had block and room numbers, a tick, a date and a second date, and **no names**, and she has said the answer to any request for a list of the people in her stock is two rooms above a betting shop on Carrow Lane. **Eleven of the hundred and twenty-two in Block C were on a lapsed term on 18 April and the water in that block was at half**, and she has said that number out loud to two people this month and not to the hundred and twenty-eight. **Rule 4(c) gives a signature three hundred and seventy-five days** — 2 April 2014 to 12 April 2015 — and she is not allowed to be angry at anybody, because nobody in those four blocks was processed. *(Wren Court is 31 rooms, 19 signed, 4 lapsed, fee £11 → £13.60. Those are Yolanda Fofana's numbers. Never Oyelaran's.)*
- **Wrote £11,280 on her own board in her own hand** — six lowland points at Tier 1 — and said she was doing it so she could look at Jonas afterwards and find out whether he would do anything with it. **He did not.**
- **She is not Rook's instrument and has never met him**, and said on the page that she has read what people write about this city and has never once seen anybody get the scale of it right: sixteen thousand eight hundred pounds is the price of a wheelie bin for two years. **She expects to lose Block C.**

## Alden Rook

- **Age / role:** 46; CivicCore operations director. A water authority man, a ledger, and right about enough to be dangerous.
- **The stairwell, Wednesday 30 April, twenty minutes, and the volume's best argument.** He says the best clause in his own document is the one that says a tier may be challenged by a district or by a node in the same tier, because the alternative is a private queue, and a private queue is a man you know, and a man you know is worse than an invoice. **He also says it is the reason a man on an embankment in April can be beaten by an invoice, and that he has known since March.**
- **He is not going to try to define *holder* on 19 May**, and he said so unasked, so that Jonas can say he asked. *I want you to know I am not going to do it, so that when somebody tells you the contractor is going to define holder, you can say that you asked him in a stairwell.*
- **He agreed to publish CivicCore's own narrowings on Nina Calder's form in a fortnight, unasked, and gave the real reason:** on 29 April at 23:11 the first thing that happened to that lowland at one o'clock in the morning was that a contractor's own pressure system noticed — not a person, a system — and in four months that is the most damaging line available to him and he would rather it be in his own document on page eleven with a heading.
- **He also said: in about two years somebody is going to use the register to say this city has an administrator, and he will have been right in a stairwell with nobody on his side.**
- **Unsoftened.** He is not softened, not redeemed, and does not lose an argument in this batch.

## Wendell Pryce

- **Age / role:** 38; CivicCore continuity field manager, lanyard and a CONTINUITY FIELD badge. Eleven years in the trade.
- **The Cooper's Reach panel, Wednesday 23 April:** came to a public hearing, said he was not there to make an offer, then put a written Tier 2 offer on four blocks in a side room with four people in it, with a date on it of 17 April — the night of the surge — written by somebody who did not know eleven people were in a Methodist hall at six in the morning.
- **The embankment, Wednesday 29 April, 00:20 to 01:25:** in a car with the hazards on, for fifty-five minutes, having been on the embankment since half past twelve because a borough gauge they maintain dropped and **CivicCore watch the lowland.** He offered to put the lowland spur and six points on Tier 2 in **eleven minutes**, for **£25,200**, and said three things:
  1. it works and he has done it twice;
  2. **it is not a favour — it is a purchase, and he cannot make it a favour without spending about four hundred pounds of company money on a district that cannot pay on a night when a man from the register is standing on the embankment, which makes the fastest way to get a district bought to be in the room at one o'clock in the morning when it is dark, and in two years a rota of nights**;
  3. and then, unasked: **there is no rota of nights, there is an acquisition — about two years after that, a tender for *emergency discretionary continuity, section four*, priced, awarded on a track record of discretionary actions, to a procurement officer who has never met any of them.**
- **He drove away without waiting to be answered.** He refused to soften it afterwards, said the clinic without the fee was still available until the last of June, and that there is no clinic without a fee.
- **Not the villain. The reason he is frightening is that he is right about a third of it and the third he is right about is the third that wins.**

## Dev Singh

- **Issuer of a live term; owner of the next fight.** The two handovers from 18 April are still in the crossing log and he has told three people this week.
- **The empty-crossing clause is nine days into a file with no hours on it**, and has been told *historic terms are not resourced* twice. He has eighteen months of fight in front of him.
- **He worked out, in nine days, why he never actually asked Jonas for it, and said so out loud, once:** every reason not to ask is a reason that would make Jonas the technician who owns his clause, and in about two years somebody would use Jonas to say the city has an administrator who happens to care about a bridge. **He asked for it to be written on a card in the coat and not in the shop, and said he will deny it.**
- **And he put two numbers together for Jonas to hold: nineteen days, the department's median first attendance on a failed civic hinge; and forty minutes, the number on a board in a corridor. *Write nineteen down next to forty somewhere, and do not let anybody tell you a number is a detail.***

## Ivo Bamba

- **Age / role:** 29; Saint Orra west night orderly. On since ten, not on the rota, not a holder.
- **Wrote a last verified essential use on 6-44 at about twenty past eleven on Wednesday 23 April, in about nine seconds, in biro, on the back of a laundry delivery note, with no date and no initials:** `ANYBODY WITH A DEAD BODY OR A PERSON WHO CANNOT GET IN ON THEIR OWN`.
- **He is the least-bad option for the second time in this account**, and the first hollow term in the city in nineteen years, and both of those are because of the same shift pattern.
- **His reason, and it is the best line about consent in the volume:** *I did not do it for the hospital. If I had done it for the hospital I would have written *a mortuary van* and left it there. I wrote the second half because on the fifteenth of April I was the one holding a laundry bag in a corridor with a door I had no business holding, and there is a number on a board in that building that says forty minutes, and forty minutes is not about a door. Forty minutes is about a family.*
- **Jonas told him what he had done and that it could not be withdrawn and must not be asked to be, and did not ask him to take it back, and said why.** Ivo Bamba said *then it stays* and went home to bed for eleven hours.
- **His name was removed from the first public return** by Nina Calder and he is not on any list. He is findable at a mortuary gate for a year and nowhere else.

## Carried refusals and new local figures

- **Gunnar Halvorsen** (service manager, Saint Orra west) has **£4,200** and four nodes and must write to one person by **Saturday 26 April**, and he asked a technician which, and was refused, and was told to write to the mortuary porter and find out that he was right. He also **found about nine hundred pounds in a dead 2011 participation line item on 22 April and put a second named clinician on the west roster without asking anybody**, and has not been thanked.
- **Yolanda Fofana** (54, Wren Court) told Jonas **he was not the answer to the Weir, first, in front of other people**, said the fee does not stop, and that preferences are what you have when you have not got a right. Her own signature lapsed on 1 April and the block went thin for eleven days and she told the block meeting *there was a mains matter* and has not told the thirty-one. **She predicted he would come back on Sunday and told him to come and not to pretend it was for the file.**
- **Margo Doré** (63) refused him on 21 April in a kitchen; made him write a refusal down in full and read it back; said a woman of sixty-three burnt a water-authority letter in March about her own supply and would not say what was in it; told him to say a sentence in a fortnight in a room where it matters; **at half past one on 30 April he said it in her kitchen and she made him promise not to come up the path at two in the morning without something that cannot wait.** And she said she wants the trap left packed.
- **Perdita Sow** (44), **out of hospital Monday 21 April**, after three nights at Saint Orra east, with a sling on her right hand, a dislocated finger and eleven weeks ahead of her, on the road on a Monday with a shopping bag because Monday is not Sunday and the borough gave her a day: *Five weeks. Every single thing you have done has ended up on a piece of paper that somebody in a building two miles from here is going to read out loud in a room. And there is a woman on this street who has been counting the doors since 1994 and has not written one of them down, and a boy of seventeen who is on a water rota and does not know what a claim is, and me. And that is the list.*
- **Prue Calloway** (58), borough safety panel chair, eleven years, used section nine of the panel rules for the first time in her career and asked for it to be minuted, and gave the finding that hands Volume 03 its door: *a building has an address. It is the people who have no location of record, and a panel cannot weigh a claim from a person it cannot locate.*
- **Mina Okafor** put the deferred-node board line in the public box on 23 April with the time and who put it up, and said she had decided at a quarter to eight in the morning that it is not an event, and asked somebody to tell her she was wrong, and nobody did.

# Character State — After Chapter 70 (VOLUME 02, BATCH 0002)

## Jonas Mercer

- **Age / role:** 32; NDC field technician, grade III, probationary, no appointment, no cabinet, no gate-initiation rights at 6-41. **On the register of attachment as LAST WORKING SYSTEM ADMINISTRATOR, CITY OF NACRE — civic standing, released by no person.**
- **Power: Stage 2, unchanged in capability, and for the first time in five weeks he performed no civic edit at all.** He **refused a money question for the fourth time in five weeks** (Halvorsen, in a doorway on 9 May) and, on 27 April at a bridge in Saint Orra, was asked a direct question by a man with a laminated card and answered it truthfully **including the sentence he had promised never to say**, and did not telephone the man it belonged to.
- **He performed the first transfer in the series that works (Ch 68)** — a held claim, 6-L/16's outfall inspection duty, moved from a lapsed node to Royden Achebe in his own name, at a hinge he does not own, with a consenting named holder, one named witness, **a second witness field reading NIL**, an unpaid claim, and **a record that names him as the man who moved it.** The issuer is not him. He cannot take it back. He learned on the page that the difference between the mover and the receiver is the whole of the cost, and that it is not a gift.
- **His insight of the batch: A DUTY IS NOT A PLACE.** An outfall is not a water point. A duty is an act, and an act can be held by a findable person in a findable office, because the holding puts no address, no household and no person into a record. **This is not a recognition of a street or of its people and must never be slid into one.**
- **Body:** unchanged. Seam mark past the elbow into the upper arm; right hand numb to the elbow and will not close; a roofing slate and a forearm for the whole of a mend.
- **What he did with the number.** He did not put it on a card, in a claim, or in a speech. He put it on the back of a departmental form with its source and a date on it and gave it to a chair in a corridor at ten to eight on the morning of 19 May, so that when he read it out in a gallery at eleven minutes past eleven **he was reading a document that had existed since 28 April in somebody else's hand.** *It is on the record before it is said, which is the only way he has found to say a number in a room without becoming the man who counted.*
- **Flaw in action, named in this batch by Bea Osunde, by Nell Ardent, by Sanaa Iqbal, by Priya Ranganathan, by Tomas Renn and by himself.** He spent 27 April giving a stranger a sentence Dev Singh had asked him never to repeat; he spent 8 May writing a number that prices a water point he has never asked the woman who keeps the street about; and he sat in a car on an embankment for nineteen minutes on 18 May and did not go up the path and did not telephone. *That is the third time I have kept a promise in the exact way that breaks it.*
- **He asked one question in a public room in eleven chapters** and it was the number, and the chair answered it honestly and could not fix it.

## Dr. Sanaa Iqbal

- **Age / role:** 35; Saint Orra emergency physician. Named on-call clinician in the gate's fallback clause. **The ninth line is still refused.**
- **A corridor at ten past four on Thursday 8 May, twenty minutes, at her initiative.** Goal on Jonas's side: nothing. He had no reason to be there for the first time in five weeks.
- **She did the second boring thing.** The bench steriliser in the decontamination room on level zero lost its supplier's service contract at midnight on 30 April; £1,100 for the year out of an activity budget whose only money was the £913 that bought the second clinician. **She found £410 — quarterly service plus a logged weekly chamber temperature verification — and named the cost honestly: twenty minutes a week, in a corridor, on a rota with a hole in it.**
- **THE FIX AND THE DISEASE, AGAIN, AND NOW WITH A PRICE ON IT.** Gunnar Halvorsen has signed the £410 and has written to the education office suspending the part-time on-call clinician's line **from 1 June**, and has told her in person at nine on Monday morning rather than on a telephone. She was not thanked for the £410 and said so in advance, and stopped him saying *noted*: *you are not allowed to write that down and put it in a coat.*
- **THE JUNE RECKONING'S DATE, GIVEN AS INFORMATION AND NOT AS A REQUEST: MONDAY 9 JUNE 2014, TEN IN THE MORNING.** A review of the west clinic's own witness structure, chaired by her because she signed the renewal clause that needs two people in a corridor at ten at night, nine people in the room, four of them on that roster. **He is not on it and there is nothing on it for him, and she gave him the date four weeks early so that he could not ask her for it in a corridor in June.**
- **State:** not reconciled, not closed, not thanked, and the second clinician is paid for until 31 May by nine hundred pounds from 2011 and after that by nothing.

## Fenella Marsh — chair of the Standing Committee on Civic Continuity

- **Refused Jonas the papers in a corridor in one sentence and it was not unkind** — not because he is not a party, which she thinks is a bad ground, but because a man with a lanyard will ring within the hour and the truth is the better answer. She has never once said *not yet* to him. She has said *no*, and the no has no review in it.
- **Refused to rule on the tabling discrepancy** and said why, and that about four times in five this happens and does nothing, and about once in five somebody moves it and gets it, and by June the city has adopted a price list as a schedule of its own standing committee.
- **19 May: let a definition of *holder* be offered from the contractor's own glossary, refused to stop the man who wanted it, and watched the registrar kill it in eleven seconds and the mover withdraw.** Then recorded, in the mover's own words, that the Committee is **unable to define the term *holder*.**
- **Made two determinations, and they are the only reason the hearing is worth reading in September: the Return of a Deferred Node is RECEIVED and not adopted; and every party holding continuity is REQUIRED to answer one in public by the next sitting, with no-party answers recorded in those words.**
- **Said the sentence the volume turns on, out loud, in a room, having read it four times in a meter room: A PARTY THAT ANSWERS MAY BE ASKED WHAT IT WILL DO, AND NOT WHAT IT WILL COST.**
- **Refused to require a person at six lowland water points and asked for that to be minuted.** She has never met Jonas Mercer before 19 May and gave him a procedure in a corridor instead of a refusal.

## Oren Pell, 61, deputy registrar, nineteen years

- **Would not tell Jonas what Rook said in the pre-sitting** and said why: *I was in that room for forty minutes and there is no minute of it, and nobody in this city can tell you what was said afterwards, including the man who said it.* Also refused to let Jonas's number become a departmental figure: **the nineteen-day median is a laminated card in a dispatch office and if a member puts it in their mouth as a city figure the department will be asked to produce it.**
- **Told him, before it happened, exactly what the register buys in a public room: nothing, and if somebody puts a microphone on him he will stand up and say so.**
- **On 19 May he leaned forward an inch and advised the chair in eleven seconds, and it is the single most consequential act of the day: a definition given in the course of considering a document is a determination of that document, and if it is minuted the Committee will have adopted a four-hundred-and-sixty-page schedule without a division and nobody will have voted on it.** He wrote nothing for eleven minutes afterwards and did not start.
- He is on Jonas's side of the argument and against the city's convenience and has still never been thanked.

## Nina Calder, records supervisor, nineteen years, she/her

- **Made the Return of a Deferred Node a public document on 7 May**, having decided on the Sunday, because a trade body had a photocopy of the whole page with the crest on it within eight days of a form being printed for a records office. *A form with a blank line at the bottom is honest. A form no party is required to answer is also a form four parties can decline to answer for as long as they like, and one a trade body can hold a copy of.* She is the woman who invented *released by no person* and she has now made a document public that can hurt a person, and she did not sleep about it.
- **Said the sentence that undoes her own form: my form is how my plate got falsified inside four days by nobody doing anything wrong.**
- **Printed SECOND WITNESS: NIL** on the first transfer record in nineteen years because it is the truth, and **refused the word register** for it: a register is a list, and there will be forty of them in nine years and by then it will be a list and by then she will not be here.
- **Said the word *nobody* out loud from the public seats of the 19 May hearing**, having had the form since 20 April and having waited nineteen days for a chair to ask her the question, and said she would write it into the form on 20 May in her own words. **That is the 20 May coda's origin and it belongs to her and not to the chair.**
- **Put Rook's Wednesday-night stairwell prediction into the papers' background field on 30 April with his name and a date on it, because she will not state a true thing without saying whose it was, and it cannot be taken out of the print, and it is in the public papers of the Standing Committee.**

## Marguerite Oyelaran, 47, chief officer, eleven years, no assistant

- **Lost her afternoon on 8 May and has not got it back.** A four-page circular with a paragraph number in it and a one-page letter signed by two people she has worked with for eleven years ending *we do not consider that a fee recoverable from rents can be defended in a public document without an answer to a question we have not been able to ask.* A councillor's office asking **whether the association should be in the room at all**, on the record, in a council chamber, unanswered by seven members. **And she did not go into the Methodist hall on her own road, where eleven households have been living at her expense since 17 April, and a woman who telephoned on Monday was not called back until Monday 22 May.** *In three weeks I will say the fee does not stop, and it will not be true on Monday, because I will not have been in that hall.*
- **Said the £305.60 out loud before he could:** Block C is a void, thirty rooms, £4,056 a year of income that has stopped, the shortfall goes from three hundred and five pounds to four thousand three hundred and sixty-one pounds and sixty pence, and the void allowance is nil in October. *Do not do that.*
- **Said the thing about the twelve:** *a data set is when somebody else makes the list. Those twelve people are making their own list, in their own handwriting, on their own doorways, on the same day, and I have been doing this for eleven years and I have never once seen it.*
- **Said the thing about consumption** without being asked and it is the chapter: the term is sized on eleven days in March when the blocks had voids in them, and April was a hundred per cent, and the difference is in four invoices going out on Wednesday to a hundred and twenty-eight people and is not in a letter.
- **Signed a man's name onto a page on 8 May** because his block is on a photocopy and being outside the agreement is worse than being inside it, and said so on the steps on 19 May: *I would have done the wrong thing too.*
- **Stated £16,800 twice in a public room at the chair's request on 19 May and asked that it be minuted exactly as she said it both times.**
- **Did not withdraw her objection to the number.** *The fourth statement is the only sentence anybody has said to me in six weeks that I did not have to work out the second half of on my own.*

## Alden Rook, 46, CivicCore operations director

- **Kept his word. He did not define *holder* in a room where the chair did not stop the man who tried, and he made the volume's best argument in four minutes, and it failed for the reason that matters: the schedule does not price urgent care and there is no instrument in the city that can.**
- **Was right about the chair** — she did not stop them, exactly as he said in a stairwell on 30 April — **and wrong about who would stop the definition.** It was the registrar, on filing grounds, and it was his own glossary that set the trap.
- **CivicCore placed two of its own nodes on schedules with its own money** — 6-44 at Tier 2 on 11 May, and 6-L/16 the lowland spur at Tier 1 on 12 May — and put them on the city's own form, as it said it would in a stairwell.
- Not softened, not redeemed, and he does not lose an argument.

## Gunnar Halvorsen, service manager, Saint Orra west, nineteen years in post

- **Made the decision nobody voted for**, on 10 May, at twenty to one, with a folder: **Tier 2, £4,200, on 6-44, the mortuary van gate, to 06:00 on Sunday 12 October.** And he could not have named his choice at eight that morning.
- **Four documents on a table and three of them said the four things were not services** — *this is a stair*; *nobody has ever asked me what it is for and I have assumed it is a barrier*; *this is a pipe in a building, I hold its maintenance, I am taking it off the list* — **and the fourth was a porter who did not know he had written the four words and who said, *that is mine, is it — right, then I would like it left where it is and I would like it not to be on a form.***
- **Read the standing continuity authorisation for the fourth time in a fortnight and saw the word *plate* in it for the first time in nineteen years**, and understood that a schedule is a chain and a chain has two other things on it that are not nodes.
- **The decontamination room.** £1,100 or nothing, and the £4,200 cannot help because a continuity fee buys a node and a supplier's contract is not a node. He signed the £410, wrote to the education office suspending the second clinician's line from **1 June**, wrote twenty minutes a week into a corridor rota with nobody against it, **and has not asked anybody about anything, because every time he asks one of those four people about a date one of them ends up on a rota because of the asking.** He will tell Sanaa in person and will not telephone her.
- **His standing rule, given to Jonas once and not to be broken: you may tell them. I would rather they heard it from somebody who is not the man with the money.**
- And of Jonas: *I asked you on 21 April and got no in ninety seconds, and I have thought about that every day since including today.*

## Royden Achebe, 49, NDC field services manager, holder of the interim lowland post in his own name

- **Holds two things in his own name: the 6-L/14 chamber-and-bank unclaimed burden (report due 29 May) and, since 17 May, the outfall inspection duty, transferred to him, which is the first transfer in this series that has succeeded.**
- **He asked for the cost to be written into the terms in Jonas's own words** — *moved by: Mercer, J.* — so that in August he can point at a piece of paper and not at a memory. In four months he will say *ask the man who moved it* and Jonas will get a telephone call.
- **He cannot give it back.** Offered inside the first hour of the seven-day window; the offer is recorded and does not transfer; the claim is released only when a successor consents; and a person who has not been asked may not be named. **The only door out is to make somebody findable and he is not going to do that.**
- **His sentence, which is different from the one he said in April and he says so: *I would rather have had it on the twenty-ninth of April. In April I was refusing a thing. This week I am asking to give one back, and asking puts a date and a name and a shape on me, and this is the first one where the shape is me and the name is also me.*** He picked up a watering can.

## Priya Ranganathan, 41, part-time, two days a week, on the west roster since 2 May, a daughter of eleven

- **Opened the care entrance on Thursday 15 May at 22:10, declaring the ninth emergency opening of the month in about seventy seconds** — for the first time in five weeks the door was opened by a person who was neither Ruth Nwosu nor Bram Osei nor Ezra Mbeki nor a declaration. She was not rostered for the night; she came because a handover needs two named people.
- **Read the five lines back unasked, got one wrong, was corrected by a porter of twenty-six, and took it.**
- **Refuses to be thanked, in a corridor, in advance: *being thanked for turning up to the witness requirement of your own job is a kind of thanks that stops a person coming back.***
- **Asked the question nobody has asked — WHAT IS A DECLINING REDUCTION — and worked the mechanism out standing at a plate: two cliffs and no scale between them; the term read on 4 October ends at the exact minute the schedule expires; the term read on 11 October begins an hour after the money stops, so the 11 October handover is the crossing and it is a Saturday night nobody has been warned about; and if it does not happen then on 12 October the door serves a rota that does not exist, and the fallback names a route and not a man, and a route is a door and a door is not a person.** Jonas had the two words and said only that; she said *I did not think you were going to.*
- **Named the answer nobody wanted: nobody is going to offer, and she gave each of the four a separate correct reason, including that she is not going to be the person who asks Bram Osei for a second refusal on a Sunday so that there are two of them on a board.**
- **Her sentence to Jonas is the sentence Sanaa Iqbal gave her in April: write it down and do not do anything with it.**

## Tomas Renn, 44, shop steward

- **His fourth question has a date on it for the first time in four months, and the date is SATURDAY 11 OCTOBER 2014 and not the twelfth:** the 22:00 handover on Saturday the fourth read a term that is the last one in that building existing entirely inside a funded schedule, and the handover on the eleventh reads a term that begins one hour after the money stops, and nobody in the corridor knows that. He is going to ask it in the shop on **Monday 19 May** in front of about nine people, with Ada against him and Cuthbert abstaining, and then go and stand in a corridor in Saint Orra west on **Thursday 22 May** and say the date out loud to the four of them.
- **Was not in the room on 19 May, as he asked, and Jonas did not come, and both facts are on the page.** A member asked that the minute record that the author of the document the contractor relies on is not present.
- **Told Jonas not to come into the west site on the 22nd or the 29th or any day between, and that if he needs him he will ask in a way that can be refused.**
- **And the cost of the batch, in his own words: the fact that you have a fourth question with a date on it and no plan attached to it is the first honest thing anybody has handed me since the eighteenth of April, and I am not going to thank you for it, and I would like it noted that I noticed.**

## Nell Ardent, 39, Open Covenants Legal Clinic

- **Said one sentence in a gallery on 19 May, allowed without motion or notice, and it is in the minute:** *the Committee is asked to note that the only instrument in this city capable of producing the number it has been asked about was printed on the thirtieth of April and has no adoption behind it.* She gave Jonas the sentence in advance on 7 May and then **refused to give it to him twice, and will not be thanked for it in a corridor, because if she is thanked in a corridor on Monday then she has been part of something.**
- **On Carrow Lane: a mass withdrawal is a data set, a withdrawal rate is a number a landlord and a funder use, and in fourteen months somebody will say the block was a bad asset with a number in it.** And the thing about a duty: a duty can be transferred without giving a street an address; an outfall is not a water point; a category is not a holder; an instrument is not an advocate; and a person is a person and the rest of it is advocacy.
- **She has refused the nineteenth of May twice and has been in a room once in this batch, for a sentence, and does not want it to become a partnership.**

## The flood forum and the roll

**GARETH RAYNOR-HALE**, about 50, resilience officer, lanyard, a card that gets him into about nine buildings and one he should not have been in. **Asks a second question, which is not about a seat, and says where every answer came from, in the room, for the minutes.** **MARTYN CRADDOCK**, 44, chair of the Saint Orra and District Flood Forum, longest-serving member since March. **The roll is a list and it keeps Nora Bell's name on it, and the eleventh place is empty and is not written *vacant*, and the minuted justification is that a room where people only put their names down when they are certain is the wrong room.** **NORA BELL, about sixty, nineteen years a crossing guard, took the eleventh place at 16:10 and handed it back at 16:25 and asked for her name to be taken off the roll, and it is not, and her words are in the minutes unedited: *I took a place at about ten past four and I gave it back at a quarter past four, and I am not sorry about either, and I would like it recorded that a crossing is not a body and that I was not asked whether I wanted to be a body.*** She also gave a man with a laminated card **nine hundred and forty** — nineteen years of pencil marks, the number of *times* somebody has stood at that barrier end and been unable to cross — and has said the number of people is not on the page and she has never tried to work it out. **Her name is in the September quarterly report.**

- **DERMOT FAHEY**, facilities supervisor, six years: *this is a stair.*
- **INES TARRANT**, car park supervisor, eleven years: *nobody in this car park who is a customer, they are all staff, and I have been doing this job for eleven years and nobody has ever asked me what it is for and I have assumed it is a barrier.*
- **RONAN VASQUEZ**, estates office, eleven years: *THIS IS A PIPE IN A BUILDING. IT IS NOT A SERVICE. I HOLD ITS MAINTENANCE. I AM TAKING IT OFF THE LIST* — and he took it off the list in nine minutes under his own holding, because the schedule lets the party holding the maintenance take a node off as well as put one on. And: *it expires on a Sunday. Every site in this borough expires on a Sunday. I have been putting these on for eleven years and I have never once had to think about what a Sunday is, because the last three times it has expired nobody in the building was standing there on the Sunday.*
- **The mortuary porter, 61, thirty-four years**, came to a table at half past ten on 10 May and did not know he had written the four words, and asked whether it was his, and said *right*, and asked for it to be left where it is and not to be on a form. **Minuted: attended, declined to sign.** His letter of 30 April, signed and dated: *I still have not got the people who do not come in a van.*
- **FRANCES TOLLEY**, committee clerk, twenty-two years: wrote the fourth sentence of the cover note on purpose, will not let a man put a paper under a door, and told the gallery fills at about eleven and the press list is not checked at the door.

- **The other three members of the committee** — Hargreaves, Petrie Okonjo, Denman — have said nothing that anybody will quote and one of them asked that the minute record that the union's author is not in the room.
- **There is only one Marguerite and one chair called Fenella Marsh and one clerk called Frances Tolley. Do not create a second of any of them.**
