# Character State — After Chapter 80 (VOLUME 02, BATCH 0003, THE HEAT)

## Jonas Mercer

- **Age / role:** 32; NDC field technician, grade III, probationary, no appointment, no cabinet, no gate-initiation rights at 6-41. **On the register of attachment as LAST WORKING SYSTEM ADMINISTRATOR, CITY OF NACRE — civic standing, released by no person.**
- **Power: Stage 2, unchanged. He performed no civic edit in this batch.** He attempted one repeat transfer on 24 May and the person it was for refused it, in three correct reasons, and the registrar's answer was that the record has no field for it and the entry is made twice and nobody is blamed. **His name is on that file a second time, at Nina Calder's insistence and against his own preference, and she told him why: the two entries are incompatible and the file will not know the difference and he will not be able to prove it is not true.**
- **What he did in this batch, and it is the volume's method:** he found out what a heat protocol measures before it measured anything, and found that the number in it is a fact about a weather station four miles away and not about a district, and that there is no instrument in this city that will record the temperature on a street. He read a form that has a hole in it and a box that will only take a number. He stood at the back of a hall with about forty people in it and said nine words in an hour and a quarter. He sat at the back of a review for eighty minutes, was given one question, and used it on a steriliser log. He went up a path on a Sunday morning unasked with nothing to do and told a woman a thing he had put in a minute without asking her, and was told he was not forgiven and was not angry with him.
- **The flaw in action, named this batch by four people:** Bea Osunde, that he has never in four months been in a position where doing nothing was the correct thing and she has not got a useful thing to say about it; Marguerite Oyelaran, that a promise kept exactly as written is worse than a promise broken; Emeka Rusk, that helping is what he has been doing and helping does not go on a form; and himself, in a shop book, that every repair in the week was correct and the district ran out of water anyway.
- **The recognition he was owed and has now paid, dramatised and not narrated, in a yard, on a coping stone, in thirty-one degrees:** the price was chosen in daylight, at a table, by a man with a budget, for good reasons, and it was the only door in the room, and Jonas's part was to do nothing, correctly, and then to sit with why the doing-nothing was the whole of what he had. He did not say the word *schedule* in his own head as a lesson and he does not say it now.
- **Body:** unchanged. Seam mark past the elbow into the upper arm; right hand numb to the elbow and will not close; a roofing slate and a forearm for the whole of a mend. He put his hand flat on a form in Halvorsen's office the way he puts it on a sill, and read four fields off it, and worked out two dates, and said nothing about either.
- **Change:** he has learned that **being the only person anybody will say yes to is not a skill and is not a service**, and that the price of being it is that four people are worse off and a fifth gets thanked for something he did not do.

## Dr. Sanaa Iqbal

- **Age / role:** 35; Saint Orra emergency physician. Named on-call clinician in the gate's fallback clause. **The ninth line is still refused.** Chaired the witness-structure review on 9 June.
- **She was told in person, on foot, in daylight, with the letter in her hand, at ten past eight on Friday 30 May**, after eleven days of waiting, by a service manager who said he was not asking her for anything and had not asked her for anything since 9 May. She said thank you for telling me and then said, in the next breath, *I am not thanking you. Those are the words.*
- **Her sentence, and it is the batch's best correction of a good instinct:** the rule in that building that stops anybody asking anybody about a date is a good rule and a correct rule, and it means nobody ever tells anybody anything, **and the people it protects are the four people and not the twenty thousand.**
- **She refused to be the standing name on twenty minutes a week, and said out loud that she could do it, and gave the reason, and the reason is the finding:** if her name is against it, twenty minutes a week has got a person on it, that person is a doctor, and she is the one already in the building at eleven at night, and then it is a rota with one name on it, and a rota with one name on it is what everybody has been refusing for four months. **The log has carried no signature since 9 May and the verification has not happened once and the quarterly visit is in July and nobody has been thanked and nobody has been argued out of anything.**
- **She did not defend her own design and said so in the first thirty seconds**, and she gave the other half of the finding before the finding: **The forty hours are the failure, and she says so first, in those words.** 06:00 Tuesday the fifteenth of April to 22:00 Wednesday the sixteenth, 2014: a woman of eighty-four in bay six for the whole of it, a man of eighty-one who wanted his own sheets, about forty other people, and she signed the clause. **And eight days later, on the night of Wednesday the twenty-third of April, the same structure did the other thing.** Not despite. Because of., and not despite but because of. A witness arrangement is a promise made by people who are tired at ten at night; it is the only kind of promise anybody in this city has been able to make; **she would rather have the practice than the service, because the practice can be refused and the service cannot, and she has read all four hundred and sixty pages and page nine is a good sentence and it is the sentence that has made a person never in the way.**
- **What she asked for is a record and not a rota**, and its fourth line must say that the practice is not a service, is unpaid, and that any proposal to make it a service must come back to that table. And: **she would rather somebody write a schedule on the first surge than make a promise at ten at night.** That is her position and it is on the record and it is not softened.
- **State:** not reconciled, not closed, not thanked. Romance has not begun and may not.

## Gunnar Halvorsen, service manager, Saint Orra west, nineteen years in post

- **On Tuesday 26 May at ten in the morning, in daylight, at a table, with a form and a crest on it, he spent £1,880 of £2,140 to put 6-51 on Tier 1 from 1 June, and he said twice that it is the only door in the room, and he was right and everybody agreed he was right.** £260 left.
- **He gave the three alternatives unsoftened** — a tanker at about £600 a load with no budget line, requisitioning that takes four days and a board that meets on Thursdays, and do nothing, which is Monday, and Monday was eight hours — and he said he had thought about it on Monday night and had been frightened of it all night and was going to do it anyway.
- **He said, unasked and in advance, that a continuity fee buys a node and is not an hour of anybody's time, and that if anybody in that building ever tells a member of staff this fee has paid for a gap in a rota then they are lying and he will deny having heard it.** The gap is still a gap. **He did not ask Jonas for anything, said so twice, and offered him the witness line instead and got nothing and went and read his plate.**
- **He told Sanaa Iqbal in person on 30 May and was not thanked, and he has not asked anybody about the twenty minutes a week since 9 May, and the log has carried no name since 9 May.** He is the reason the log is empty and he is not the villain for it.
- **His decision is Thursday 29 May: the 11:00–13:30 gap out of £260.** He gave Jonas the date and refused to tell him which place he would not be in, and said he would let him find out from the transcript in about nine days. **He is still the man who asked a money question in a doorway on 21 April and got no in ninety seconds and has thought about it every day since, including that morning, and he said so out loud to Jonas while handing him a form.**

## Marguerite Oyelaran, 47, chief officer, eleven years, no assistant

- **Her answer to the heat protocol went in without her on Thursday 28 May at about twenty past four in the afternoon, in the correct order, in biro, by a part-time clerk of sixty-one: 106, and her name and the ring number.** A form is a public document on completion. It was recorded at 16:20 and it cannot be unsaid.
- **The harm is exact and she worked it out before anybody queried it, and it is worse than the obvious reading.** 128 rooms · **122 on the rent roll** (six never signed) · **106 occupied** (22 households moved out) · **92 rooms the association is actually paid for** (Block C's thirty have been on a void allowance since 6 May) and the shortfall is £4,361.60. **The only difference the two public numbers show anybody is sixteen — sixteen rooms on a rent roll with nobody in them — and sixteen is a void, it is a landlord's exposure figure, and it reads as bad management, and her own sentence is *the legible difference is sixteen and sixteen is void and void is my fault*. 106 minus 92 is fourteen, and eight of those fourteen are the eight households still in Block C carrying water for thirty rooms since 1998 and six are the six who never signed, and those are the only two numbers anybody would recognise as hardship and the only two that cannot be on anything, because every document that could hold them is a list of who does not pay.** She will not produce a list.
- **She has refused three times this week to give the breakdown of the sixteen and will not produce a list.** The answer to any request for a list of the people in her stock is two rooms above a betting shop on Carrow Lane and that line is in her own file from 2016. She has told nobody about the six.
- **She has not stopped the £2.60 on the eight Block C households and will not, and she said why in a yard, and it is not a moral reason: refunding them would mean admitting in writing that a service in one of her four blocks has stopped, and a service that stops is a node that goes into failure, and a node in failure is a thing this city has a document about. She would rather be hated for it than find out in August what she has done by stopping it.** Ivy Marsden said it was the first straight answer she has had about that money.
- **On Saturday 31 May, in the Methodist hall, about forty people, she said THE FEE DOES NOT STOP, once, in four minutes, having lost Block C and a quarter of a return and a whole afternoon.** She told the room there are twelve households who have asked to leave and that twelve is a number and not a group and she would not say which ones, and she did not tell the room clause 4(c) exists and said in advance on the Friday that she would not.
- **She raised £11,280 in that hall herself and said the sentence she could not finish on the nineteenth:** the minute says six lowland water points and nobody in this city can say which six, and if nobody can say which six the water points are, then nobody can say whose six they are either, and **the chair who read the number out** on 19 May did it without asking anybody, and she has had nine days and has not decided whether she can live with that. **She was in the gallery on 19 May. She heard the chair read it, and Jonas Mercer corrected the attribution in the hall — he wrote down a number she wrote first, a chair read it out, he did not choose the six, and he has never been able to find out who the six are.**
- **She refused to have Block C looked at, and the reason is the shape of this volume: the day she looks at it is the day it is a record, and it is already a record, and if somebody comes into that meter room with a camera then she has a photograph of a room with a council crest on the wall, and a crest on a wall is the beginning of a circular, and she has had two of those in eleven years.**
- **She is not Rook's instrument and has never met him. She expects to lose Block C and has said so in writing. £4,361.60 short. Void allowance nil in October. She pays her own salary out of her own pocket since 2011.**
- **The sentence she has been carrying since 28 April, said at last in a corridor on Friday 22 May: I do not know which of the two I am more afraid of. I am afraid of the four thousand three hundred and sixty-one pounds and sixty, because in November there is no money and four blocks have no water. And I am more afraid of the other one, which is that in two years this association is a number — a hundred and six rooms, or ninety-eight, or however many are left — and a number is the only thing anybody can be measured on, and I did the measuring.**

## Royden Achebe, 49, NDC field services manager, holder of the interim lowland post in his own name

- **Holds two things in his own name: the 6-L/14 chamber-and-bank unclaimed burden, and, since 17 May, the outfall inspection duty on 6-L/16.** He has now been the holder of one of them for eight days without being at the place on the day it had to be done, and he could not send anybody, and he said *the duty waits, and I would be grateful if you did not do anything about it.*
- **He offered the outfall duty back inside the first hour of a seven-day window on 18 May and used no minute of the rest of it.** His seven-day window expired on 25 May unused. **He was not released and could not be.**
- **On 24 May he wrote down a fact nobody had asked for and nobody has answered: the department will accept the 6-L/14 report at about level three, which is a tray, about eleven weeks, and a signature — and what that creates is not a vacancy, it is a line with his name in it and `not released` in the next column. A line like that does not sit on a file for a year. Lines like that get found.** He is in a corridor at Gantry Ward with a cabinet and a drawer.
- **He refuses to have 6-L/14 named a street, and says the reason there is not one is the correct reason.** He is not permitted to name a successor; a burden cannot be refused; a claim can only be released to a successor who consents; and there is no party that answers for 6-L/14 and there has not been one since 6 April.
- **He filed his nine hundred words on 29 May at eleven o'clock with nobody from this account in the room, which he arranged himself in nine words on a telephone on the Wednesday.** He is two men worse off, in two files, in two buildings, and neither file knows the other exists, and he read the four lines of the last page out loud in a works van doorway on the tide and said he had looked for a way to name a street for eight weeks and there is not one.
- **In August somebody will ring Jonas Mercer about a Tuesday and the man who will ring him is Achebe, and Achebe has known it since 18 May, and Jonas has not yet worked out whether he is going to be the one who answers.**

## Emeka Rusk, 51, pump operator, docks, twenty-six years

- **Refused the repeat transfer of the outfall inspection duty on 24 May, in three correct reasons, and refused the thing he was offered instead.** If he holds it, the £1,880 node is his and he cannot ring the company. He will not have Achebe handed a thing that has already been handed about once, and neither man asked him. And a duty cannot be half-shared: if he holds it Achebe is out, and helping is what he has been doing since 2 April, and helping does not go on a form and is why nobody counts it.
- **What he asked for instead is that the duty be recorded, and he does not want it on a form.** He has had a month of working it out alone on Saturday mornings with nobody asking him questions, and he says that is the only thing he has got out of the last month.
- **He has entered twenty-seven faults in his own hand since 2 April with the operator box left blank, and he left it blank again on 24 May, and he is a witness on a record and is not a holder and is not a witness to the second entry.** He is not on the new entry. Nina Calder wrote that in deliberately: *NOT A HOLDER. NOT A WITNESS TO THIS ENTRY.*
- **He still has not been paid and did not ask and will not.** He gave a third of a bottle of water to a man at the top of a slipway at about ten to nine in the morning and neither of them made a thing of it.

## Margo Doré, 63, Weir

- **Was told on Sunday 1 June, at about eleven, on foot, in the sun, that a Tier 1 price on six lowland water points is in a Committee minute, and that one of the six is the stand at the top of the slip, and that the chair said the Committee would not make a person at six water points on a lowland and would like it minuted that she was asked to and declined in the only words available.** She had not been asked and had been waiting thirteen days to find out whether anybody in this city would ask her a question before asking a question about her.
- **She said two things in a fixed order. One: you have not done it again and you have done it worse — you kept the sentence and you used it on my water in a room without me, and the price came with it in your mouth. Two, and she wanted it said out loud: I am not angry with you, because you did what you said you would do, I would have said no, my no would have been eleven words and would not have been in a minute, and in September the sentence on the paper will be mine and it will have been in a room.**
- **She poured two cups, which she has not done since 30 April, and did not offer him any information about the six, and he did not ask, and neither of them said the word *schedule* in that kitchen.**
- **She refused a pump in advance, in her own words, in the kitchen, to a man who came for nothing and not to a pump, and nobody argued and no pump exists.** A man will come up the path in about two months with a van and a clipboard and a scheme and a photograph of a stand, and he will be correct, and the water will come, and she will say no, because a pump is a thing and a thing can be bought and the day this street has a pump somebody is going to ask what it is attached to, and the answer will be a paper, and the paper will have one of her neighbours' names in a field on it, because that is how any of them has kept a door open since 3 April. She would like it in the record that she said it on the first of June, in advance, and not to a pump.
- **The three positions stand. The ring of pencil has nothing in it. Nobody was on the rota, because there is no rota. Bo Trimble said there is no water, was told he is not going to fix it, said right, and went home, and nothing was added to him.**
- **The thread is unpaid and unresolved. What has happened is that she has the fact and has had it since 20 May, and that is the whole of the settlement and it is not a settlement.**

## Oren Pell, 61, deputy registrar, nineteen years

- **Refused to strike a duty and refused to move it and then, in eleven seconds by telephone on 24 May, made the ruling that let a record show two things that have no field: the record has no field for a duty that is held by one person and performed by another, and where a record has no field, the entry is made twice, and nobody is blamed.**
- **On Monday 2 June he said the best thing he says in the volume and refused a cooperative steward board in one word at a volume that made a woman two floors down look out of a door, and said he was not the man who killed it.** The whole of it: a body of nine seats has one power, it may require a party to answer and receive the answer, and it cannot require a person to do anything, hold a duty, or answer a question, and there is no appeal from it, and the reason there is no appeal is page nine — a tier may not be challenged by a person. So the ninth seat is a chair. Not a chair with a person in it, which is what a person always is. A chair with a person in it that nobody can ask a question. **A steward board whose ninth seat cannot be challenged is not a steward board. It is a register with chairs. And every one of the four hundred and sixty pages of that schedule is a register with chairs.**
- **He told the room that a chair on 7 May said the opposite of this in public and said she could not say where she got it from, and that he has been a registrar for nineteen years and has spent four months waiting for somebody in this city to say the other half of it.** He asked Frances Tolley to put his job title next to it. He is on Jonas's side of the argument and against the city's convenience and has still never been thanked.

## Nina Calder, records supervisor, nineteen years, she/her

- **Printed the batch's two instruments side by side on a Thursday with a straight edge between them and refused the sentence he brought in: they are NOT the same instrument, and if he says that in a room in September he will be wrong in front of about nine people. They have exactly one thing in common and it is the absence of a power.** She found the thing that made it a fact: the protocol's first box is a number box, with a line the width of a ruler and no ceiling on it, and a box with a line in it and no ceiling is the most dangerous object in the civic office, and she has watched two hundred men fill one in and eleven of them put *all* in it.
- **Put `moved by: MERCER, J.` on the second entry of 24 May against his objection, read it back to him before typing it, and told him why: two incompatible entries on one file, and in four months somebody will read them side by side and work out that the man who moved a duty onto a man is the reason a second man is doing a duty he does not hold, and that is not true and she will not be able to prove it is not true.**
- **Said, on 30 May, at 13:10, unasked and once: the last time there was a gap in that file it was 2011, it got filled inside about four months by a man sent out from estates, and the thing that got him the job was being told the line was plant, and he has a fortnight somewhere in this city with a bucket under a tap. That is all of it. He is not a bad man. She has worked with him for nine years and has never been able to ask him.** She asked for nothing, said the arrangement with Jonas has been in place since April, and would not see the book.
- **Found a fourth list and stopped before writing anything on it, on the Friday, and said why: a list is not a record, a record is about one thing at one time, and a list is a set of things somebody intends to go on adding to, and the intention is the danger.** A register of attachment with one name, a register of narrowings with fourteen on a public board, and a proposed board with nine seats. She would not be the fourth.

She will be there on 19 June at nine with a folder.
- **Put a laminated heat-protocol card in a drawer on 2 June, which she said is the first thing anybody has put in a drawer in that room in three weeks and it is going in a drawer because it is the only correct place for it.**

- **JONAS MERCER, 32.** Stage 2, rule mender, unchanged in capability. **He performed no mending in this batch and refused to, twice, in his own words, and the refusal is correct and is on the page.** He filled in a Return of a Deferred Node and put his name in the box that asks who is putting it in — the first time his name has gone on a public civic form — because Nina Calder said a form that has never had a person's name on it is a form that cannot tell the difference between a state and a person, and the batch needed one. **He refused a number he could have manufactured in about four minutes**, in front of a man with a printer's deadline, and said a sentence instead. He learned nothing in this batch that he wanted to learn: a chain of four valid documents, which is one placing and three assignments, a registrar's four-sentence answer, and a woman in a stairwell telling him the third condition is a person who cannot be asked. **He has not been on the agenda, not a party, not a member, not a departmental officer, and not asked anything in a public room beyond one question per scene.** He did not telephone Marguerite Oyelaran (fifth time), did not go up the Weir path, did not ring the telephone number a woman gave him on 11 July, and did not write the letter eight households have asked for twice. **The right hand is numb to the elbow and does not close; he braces the Wren Court plate with his left forearm for four minutes and does not use the right hand at all.**
- **YOLANDA FOFANA, 54.** Named steward of Wren Court, nineteen years in the block, fourteen as steward, a former ward sister. **The reader is given permission to dislike her slightly and is then not given permission to keep it.** She lies by omission in her own block meeting on 26 June because the truth requires a chain, a tier and a reference and eleven of her residents are on a lapsed term; she says out loud in the chapter that she has done it and why. She reads the chain out of a public deed register onto four sheets in her own hand — one placing and three assignments — corrects the count herself in the room (*three assignments, not four, because one of the four is a placing and a placing is not a hand*), does the arithmetic, and can defend every line of it. **She is the person who asked the volume's question out loud — who pays when a resident refuses the price — and she already had the answer and it is not the one anybody in the buildings wants.** She requires three things of Jonas before instructing the mending, one of which is that he does not do it. She said it twice, once in a workshop and once in front of twenty-nine people, and the second time is the one that was entered. **She says the fee does not stop and it does not stop, in front of thirty-one people who can all check.** Her third condition is no longer hers: it is one person, findable, holding a thing none of the thirty-one whose water it is can ask her a question about. **She has told the block about the eleven lapsed terms and about her own signature lapsing on 1 April and about not ringing a woman in flat twenty-two back for three weeks, and none of it has been forgiven and none of it was asked to be.**
- **OREN PELL, deputy registrar.** The Monday 30 June twice-standing rule is the **third** ruling of the year that is a door and not a wall; the 9 July ruling is the **fourth**, and named transfer stewardship's cost in law: a claim discharged for the holder is not discharged for the person who caused it; findability is not answerability. **He ruled on Monday 30 June that the standing must be given twice and that he would refuse to enter anything until it had been, and he did refuse, on Wednesday 2 July, at 09:04, and he wrote the date of his own refusal on the record.** The ninety-day notice went out at 11:00 on Thursday 3 July, the day of the entry, and he telephoned the shop on Monday 7 July to say what the annex-six clause says, and said the first of October is a real date and a Wednesday and twelve weeks away. He said there is no mechanism to make the top of a chain pay and none to make a person take a duty, and that those are the same sentence. He is tired since 11 June and says so. He mentioned section 11 once, in a corridor, in nine words, and refused to say anything else about it, and said he has no power to constitute anything. **He has not softened and he has not been argued out of anything.**
- **NINA CALDER, records supervisor.** **The fourth page is the arc of this batch for her and it ends in a decision she made, twice.** Five weeks of refusing to design a fourth list, one page in a pad from 5 June, the page in the bin tray on 4 July at 20:20, the page out of the bin on 7 July at 08:30, and one slip on it: a week, a place, a number, what was counted, and one sentence saying what it is not, and **a person may refuse to be counted and the count then says so and says how many refused.** She said it is the closest thing to a thing that works she has been able to design in five months and then said she has a fifth one in her head and is not writing it down, because writing it down makes it a scheme. She read a nine-item cost attachment out loud at a public counter in her flat voice. ## Chapter 100 — character state, Volume 02 Batch 0005 (Section E and the close of the volume)

- **JONAS MERCER, 32.** Stage 2, rule mender, unchanged in capability, **and a transfer steward in practice and not in title.** He performed no civic edit. He refused a decontamination log twice, out loud, to a bench, in an empty room, and the reason is the volume's own: **filling it in is a service, and a service is what the 9 June finding is against, and he is not going to be the man who signs the first line of one** — and he did not do the twenty minutes either. He **refused to chair** a board of nine on 26 September, in a corridor, with a reason: a chair is a person who decides which of two things gets heard first, section 11 does not require a chair, the ninth seat is not a chair, and in about two years somebody is going to use the word *administrator* about him in a room. He did not telephone Marguerite Oyelaran for the fifth time, did not ring the number from 11 July until 19 September when he was owed the year, did not go up the Weir path, did not ask Ivy Marsden anything in a hall she walked into, did not ask the woman with the trolley anything at a stand he has stood opposite three times, did not ring Dorothy Cresswell, did not ask Peter Naylor anything, and did not open the sealed envelope he stood six minutes in front of. He was the man who answered the telephone on Wednesday 14 August, and on 16 September he attended a duty he could not hold and put his name in a margin on a form because there is no field for the man who watched it. **He is the man who put a number in a public report on 5 September and let a woman of sixty be findable in it, deliberately, having spent a month refusing to put anybody anywhere.** Body: the seam mark runs past the elbow into the upper arm, the right hand is numb to the elbow and will not close, and on 25 September it went at the fourth line of a page and stayed gone and he wrote the rest with his left hand, and he has been meaning to mention it to somebody for a month.
- **YOLANDA FOFANA, 54, named steward of Wren Court, nineteen years in the block, fourteen as steward, ninth seat of a cooperative steward board.** The volume's second-most important person and its most exposed. **She is findable, unpaid, unaskable, and the only seat in the body that cannot be emptied by anybody else.** She filled the ninth seat in a Methodist hall in eleven minutes in an aisle and stated the whole price out loud, including that she is the one woman out of forty people there anybody can write to, and that the thirty-one whose water it is are not seated and are four hundred yards away and she is not going to pretend she is the same thing as them. **On 24 September she declined to answer Tomas Renn's question about the day after, gave the reason, and told Jonas Mercer not to write it down; he wrote down that she was told not to write it down.** On 29 September a clerk of twenty-two years asked her how it feels and she said: **it feels like the only one who can get out** — and then gave three more minutes, including the prediction that in about four years one of the eight will say something false in a room and four of them will hear it and none of them will be able to make him stop, and the last useful thing that body does will be somebody walking out, and the minute will not say anybody made him do it. **She is not frightened and she is not a heroine and she is not thanked, and she said on 4 September that thanking her would make it a thing somebody did for her.**
- **OREN PELL, 61, deputy registrar, nineteen years.** He made the ruling of 28 August, which is narrow, on a sub-substitution, and which he read out and then explained with an example and then said *nothing* about the consequences, in front of nineteen people and a transcript, because a registrar who rules on the consequences of his own ruling in the same breath has stopped being a registrar. He wrote the registrar's statement to the board himself and had it typed for nothing by a clerk. **On 22 September he came to the shop for the first time in his life, on his feet, with a sandwich on the bench, to say that he was finished saying the sentence about who pays for a refusal, and to hand Jonas Mercer a job instead of a ruling: the day you ask somebody it will be a person in a room who can say no, and when they say no that ends the ask.** He read page four of section 11 out in a corridor on 26 September and then stopped, and said he was not going to say the next sentence, and asked a clerk to minute *the next sentence was not said* and to put Calder's reason under it. He is unsoftened, he is right, and he has been the right man in six rooms this year and has been thanked in none of them.
- **NINA CALDER, records supervisor, about fifty, nineteen years in that office and designing lists since 1999 — two different numbers, and she has never confused them in public — she/her.** **She read page four of section 11 on Tuesday 19 August and told nobody, and gave the reason in a records office in front of a committee clerk and a man with a register, and was not argued out of it: a person may not be required even to be told, and a person who knows she is the only seat that can empty a board is findable in a way she is not now.** She is the first person in this city whose condition of 1 June has been minuted by anybody but herself — Frances Tolley wrote it on the back of her own hand because a clerk writes down everything. **She refused the fifth page on 1 September, in a public room, at a counter, in the right order, and nobody argued with her, and it stands.** She refused to type the letter and gave the reason: a typed letter with a crest at the top is a departmental document and a departmental document is a record and a record gets asked for by the next managing agent in four years. She produced a record of shapes with no name box on it and said *you want me to put a name on it because you think a record with no name cannot be argued with; it can; it is being argued with right now, by you, in a room, in public, and I am glad of it.* She gave Jonas Mercer Peter Naylor's name on 15 September and nothing else and told him not to use it. She has a sixth refusal in her in nineteen years and she does not call them that.
- **RONAN VASQUEZ, 48, estates office, Saint Orra west, eleven years.** **The batch's most useful ordinary person.** He signed the decontamination verification acceptance at 16:20 on Thursday 15 August in a flat sheet in a plastic wallet, having thought about it since the previous afternoon, and he put three things on the form in his own words: it is not a service, it is a person reading a strip; he has held the maintenance of that room's pipework since 2011; **if anybody makes this a rota he will stop and they can have the paragraph number instead.** He told the corridor his name goes on a log and does not go on the board and that both of those are true and neither cancels the other. He said the twenty minutes will not survive November, and said so before anybody could ask him to be careful about it. **He was offered the eighth seat on a board of nine and refused it on Friday 22 August, in a piece of paper in his own words, and he has never read section 11 and nobody has told him what is in it, and his reason is the same sentence he put on the acceptance seven days earlier.** He is named on a public sheet in the vestibule of the Old Ward, and he is the reason the eighth seat is Gloria Nye's. **He is the answer to every question the volume asked, and he is an estates supervisor who does a Sunday morning because it is a Sunday.**
- **MARGUERITE OYELARAN, 47, chief officer, eleven years, no assistant.** **She brought the case that ended the volume's central mechanism, against her own interest, told nobody, and put it on a board in a shop.** Nineteen minutes, eleven pages of transcript, and not one fact contested by the other side. She did not ask for her money back and said so into the record, and gave the reason: **£4,200 would not have fixed a riser and she worked that out in a block in April and had nobody to give it to.** She put ninety-two in a ring-number box on 4 August on purpose, and the second public number from her body is a number and not a household, and that is the reason nobody can be hurt by it this week and the reason somebody will be hurt by it in about four months and she could not say who either. She said in open session that six words were written in a records room in eleven minutes in March and accepted by a panel on 1 April, and that she has known since 2 April and has never been able to find out who wrote them and is not going to. **She and Jonas Mercer have not spoken since 31 May. Both of them have said publicly, in rooms, that this is now permanent.**
- **ALDEN ROOK, 46, CivicCore operations director.** Unsoftened and right. He did not contest a fact, asked for that to be minuted before she started, and made the volume's best argument in four minutes: *we found out; that is the whole of my case and the whole of my weakness; a paid claim is a more trustworthy claim only because the payer found out, and that is a true sentence and it is a terrible reason to price a door.* In a doorway afterwards, with the folder under his arm: **a thing that was going to happen anyway now has to be argued for**, and he is frightened not of losing the price but of the day somebody has to stand up in a room and say *we cannot afford to keep that door open* with no price on it and nobody in this city has ever had to say that sentence with their name attached. - **JONAS MERCER, 32.** Stage 2, rule mender, unchanged in capability, **and a transfer steward in practice and not in title.** On the register of attachment as LAST WORKING SYSTEM ADMINISTRATOR — civic standing, no grade, no department, not subject to review, **released by no person.** **He performed no civic edit in this batch, no mending, and attended no duty, and he did not go to Saint Orra west on the night of 3 January and did not go into the building in Gantry Ward on 22 December.** He asked **one question in every public room and one in every corridor**, and the counting is right in every chapter: **fourteen** words in a kitchen off a landing on 11 December, **eleven** at a records counter on 22 December, **five** in a housing-office corridor on 18 December, **eleven** in a records corridor on 2 January, **three** at a records counter on 15 January, **twelve** in a shop on 23 January, **one** in a vestibule on 26 January, and **none at all in the Methodist hall on 13 January, none in the hall on 21 January, none in the Saint Orra west corridor before six o'clock on 4 January, and none in the vestibule on 28 January — and he announced each of those counts himself.** **He did not go and see Royden Achebe, and the refusal is the hardest one he has made and it stands: an apology from the man who named you in a room you were not in has to be said in a room, and the only kind of room left in this borough where it could be said is somebody's kitchen, and he has not got one and is not entitled to one. He is still two men findable by his own sentences and cannot unmake either, and a third thing he did not start. **He asked nobody's standing anything and helped nobody and was thanked by nobody and asked for nothing.** Body: the seam mark runs past the elbow, the right hand is numb to the elbow and does not close, and he has still not mentioned it to anybody. **He is thirty-two.**

She has refused Frances Tolley's shape being set beside hers, and she is right. **She has still not been told that she is a door and she is not the only door in that building, and she has said twice that she will not be told, and nobody is going to tell her.** She took the letter from the hall on 3 December and it was in a handbag in a kitchen off a landing for seven weeks; on 23 January she told him it was the only piece of paper in the borough with that name on it and that she is not going to be told where the other one is and neither is he. **Nobody thanked her and nobody is going to.**
- **NINA CALDER, records supervisor, about fifty, nineteen years, she/her.** **Her seventh refusal is now on the page: on Friday 2 January 2015, at a counter, in the right order, in about eleven seconds, in four numbered parts, she refused a request from a resident of the rear block at Carrow Lane to add a one-line free-text REASON column to the register of narrowings, and the refusal stands and nobody may come back to it.** The request went back with nothing in it on 5 January. **She wrote her six refusals out once, in order, on a pad, and crossed the list and wrote under it: *seven. Stop counting.*** She said the whole method out loud to Jonas Mercer at a counter on 2 January and neither of them wrote any of it down, and she told him, in her words, that there are two of them in this borough who could put it in a file before lunch and neither is going to, **and that is the whole of what this borough has instead of a rule.** She has said her load-bearing sentence five times in the same order since April and it was said once more in a corridor in 0119 without a change of a word. **The second public record is still out, unsigned, with about four hundred other people's names on it and about eleven people having taken the extract and two having written back and been wrong, and the clerk wrote *enclosure received, no comment* and that is in the file.** The board has not moved since 26 November.
- **FRANCES TOLLEY, committee clerk, twenty-two years, sixty-one.** **She said no to Jonas Mercer in a corridor on Thursday 22 January 2015, before he had said what the question was — the fifth time — and then told him the price of the reading rule out loud, in about nine seconds, unasked, which is the first time anybody has given it: there is no way at all to say that she has not done it on a given day, and she would not want them to be able to, and forty-one minutes each way on her own time in the wind since 5 November, and nobody knows and nobody is to know. And she told him what a corridor is for: the only place in this borough with no minute, no agenda, no box, no name, no gallery and no publication, and a door in a corridor is a door a person can open on her own time for a person who turns up.** **SHE USED THE READING RULE. ONCE. On an undated day in January 2015, in a corridor at the records counter, in about eleven seconds, on Peter Naylor, 44, who was not told he was in it. She is not going to say whether it worked and nobody may ask her. Nobody told Jonas Mercer and nobody was going to; he found out at about eleven in the morning on 22 January, before he had seen her that afternoon, because the man said four words at a counter to somebody else: `I was read to.`** The one copy is still in her inside pocket. She has also said out loud, twice in a corridor, that the ninth seat's reading of the position is not hers and the two are not to be put next to each other.
- **BEVERLEY ANNIS, 54, principal, twenty-six years, four hundred and ten flats.** **Untouched and not in any room in this batch. She still has no copy of the reading rule and has not asked for one, and the reason she gave on 5 November remains entirely correct, and a Registrar is still using her building as the test case for a refusal nobody has tested her on.** A man of forty-nine is now findable through a sentence about his own conduct and she is a party who has read the determination and cannot be told what the other entry is.
- **BEATRICE OSUNDE, the shop, about sixty.** Unmoved and unimproved. **On 24 December she made him say the reason out loud, in thirty seconds, once, and did not improve it: an apology from the man who named you in a room you were not in has to be said in a room, and there is no room in this borough in which it can be said that does not also become a record, and the only kind of room left is somebody's kitchen, and he has not got one. And: in a room it happened to him and he could answer back and it would be over; in a file it is a handle. He would rather be the man who did it in a room than the man who did it in a file.** She told him to say that last part to himself four times a day for a week, because every person she has watched do it alone at night for years got it right and every one of them did it alone. And on Wednesday 24 December, when he told her he had written the reason down and not the apology: **that is what a pad is for. It is yours. There is no box on it anywhere and that is also the point.** Her sentence of 24 November is the batch's engine and it was not said again: *there are three people in this borough who need the hard one and I have watched all three of them get older this year while you were getting round to yourself.*
- **THE WOMAN OF THIRTY-FOUR AT THE BOTTOM OF QUARRY STREET — BERNICE OFORI, 34.** **On Monday 19 January 2015 a printed slip arrived at the Methodist hall from COMMITTEE SERVICES with three boxes and a line for a name, saying that if she was not present on the date her correspondence would be treated as withdrawn, and nobody in that hall sent it and nobody could. On Wednesday 21 January at about twenty past four, in daylight, in a hall with the heating off and nobody in it, SHE CAME THROUGH THE DOOR SHE PUT A LETTER THROUGH ON 28 NOVEMBER, ALONE, AND WAS NOT FOUND, WAS NOT VISITED, WAS NOT TELEPHONED, WAS ASKED FOR NOTHING AND WAS GIVEN NOTHING. She read two pieces of paper standing up in about four minutes, put no mark in any of the three boxes, and DID NOT WRITE ON THE PRINTED ONE, because a sheet with a crest and a form number and a reference is a document and her name is not going at the top of a document that nobody asked her for. She wrote on the second one instead, which is unsigned, has no heading, no box, no line for anything, and cannot be used to show anybody anything at all: her name and the street and the date, in her own hand, in biro — the first time in eleven years those four things have been together on one piece of paper, and she did it on purpose and in daylight — and then nine seconds that cost her nothing: I have not withdrawn anything. I asked a question. There is no sitting to attend and nobody has asked me to attend one. She left both pieces on the table, took nothing with her, because her own November letter was still in a handbag in a kitchen four hundred yards away, and went out at ten to five on a bus she had planned herself.** **The printed slip went back into the tray where a printed thing goes, and that sheet — four lines of the minute-taker's own biro with her four above them — is in a plastic wallet with a rubber band in the drawer of a trestle table in that hall, and there is no key, and there is no list of what is in any drawer in that building, and the only record in the world of any of it is four lines of biro. THE OTHER PIECE OF PAPER WITH HER NAME ON IT IS HER LETTER OF 28 NOVEMBER, IN A HANDBAG IN A KITCHEN OFF A LANDING, AND NEITHER IS A DOCUMENT AND NEITHER MAY BE OPENED. HER NAME IS NOT ON THE PRINTED SLIP AND MAY NOT BE PUT ON IT.** Nobody was thanked, nobody thanked anybody, and no minute in this borough records that anybody was not thanked. **Her standing is UNRESOLVED and may not be resolved.**
- **THE WOMAN WHO KEEPS THE MINUTES.** **Still unnamed in this account and still not going to be.** She has carried the whole of the last eight weeks: she found a letter in her bag for three days and worked out what a letter is; she found a name stated in a room and wrote a minute that says a name was stated and does not contain it; she put a printed slip in a tray and wrote a second unsigned note beside it and left the two on a trestle table and shut the hall and told nobody; and on 21 January, at eleven minutes past five, she read a name off a piece of paper twice, and put both pieces in a plastic wallet in a drawer, and shut the drawer, **and in about four years that drawer is the only record in the world of any of it.** She has no name on any minute and there is no box anywhere in this borough that says who wrote a thing down, and nobody has asked her since 1 December and she is not going to be told.
- **INES TARRANT, 44, car park supervisor, eleven years.** **On 28 January 2015 the ninth seat asked her why she meant it, because she had asked on 26 November to be asked and nobody in that room could require a person to answer a question, and she answered in about nine seconds and it is the only reason any of the nine has ever given: *because I have been the nearest person to a barrier for eleven years and nobody has ever asked me what it is for, and if this turns into a job then I am a woman with a job on a board and the nearest person to the barrier is a woman with a job on a board, and in about four years somebody will use that to tell me what the barrier is for. And I am still here. That is all I have got. I have not got an answer and I have got a reason.***** She has not stopped and nothing followed from it and it did not go in the minute, at her own request. Unresolved.
- **WINIFRED CRABBE, 62, linen supervisor, nineteen years.** She read the six water points out in a hall in daylight on 13 January in the voice of a woman who has read a laundry list aloud for nineteen years, and asked the board to take the price, and the registrar said no and the ninth seat said: write down that we did nothing, in the correct words.
- **GLORIA NYE, 44, self-employed heating engineer, twenty-one years.** **In January she converted the lowland's whole service floor into one sentence in front of a room: £1,880 is one boiler in a small flat, the cheapest anybody quoted her in two years was £1,790, and the reason the six of them cannot be bought at all is not that the people who need them are poor — the reason is that we are not on the map.** And on 28 January she was in a vestibule in daylight and the man of about fifty-six said he had followed all of it from a car park and could not tell what any of it was for.
- **IBRAHIM SESAY, 51, caretaker, Tarn Street school, thirty-one years, second seat.** Asked for the six lowland water points to come to the board on 13 January, got the price into the record, and said the only thing anybody could say about it: nothing.
- **DERMOT FAHEY, 33, facilities supervisor, Saint Orra west, six years.** Named the reason there is no seat for the lowland out loud, in the correct words, in a hall, and stopped a man mid-sentence on 13 January because the body cannot require anybody to do anything, including to stop talking.
- **OREN PELL, registrar, nineteen years.** **Stood in a corridor outside a room of eleven feet by nine on 26 January and did not come in, because a registrar who comes into a room of eleven feet by nine turns it into a room he was in. Gave the two sentences the volume runs on — Rook's sentence about him, and his own of 2 June — and then the third: a list of who needs it is a list of who exists, and in four years the list is in a drawer with a date on it, and the date is the day somebody asked, and the asking is the harm. And on 13 January, in a hall: the reason the lowland has no seat is correct, has been correct since the first of March, and is not going to be fixed.** He has not been asked to read the reading rule in a determination again and nobody has let him.
- **MARGARUITE OYELARAN, 47, chief officer, eleven years, no assistant, £4,361.60 on no form.** She asked for the answer to be minuted in the borough record as a thing said in a room, so the word *scope* would stand in two files in two buildings, and she said the reason out loud: *a thing that is wrong in one place and right in another is a thing that gets corrected in four years by whoever is left.* **And the price of it is a date against her name and the word *disputes*, and a list is the only instrument this borough has ever offered her, and she has made herself the person most likely to be asked for one. She has not produced a list. 106 in a ring-number box in May, 92 in August on purpose, and a difference of fourteen worked out loud in a room and now in two files, and it is a difference and not fourteen households and there is no form on which anybody could write that.** Neither of them spoke to the other in the corridor and neither is going to.
- **PETER NAYLOR, 44, level-three acceptance officer, field services, Gantry Ward, out of estates since 2011.** **He was read the two entries of the reading rule in a corridor, in about eleven seconds, on a Tuesday in January, and he was not told he was in it, and on Thursday 22 January at about a quarter past eleven he said four words at a counter to somebody else: `I was read to.` He does not know what any of the words in the entries mean and has never known, and nobody in this borough is able to ask him one question about any of it, EVER, and he is not going to be told that it happened.** He is a wall. He is not the man of forty-nine. Do not conflate them.
- **ROYDEN ACHEBE, 49, NDC field services manager.** **STILL NOT TOLD, and nobody told him, and Jonas Mercer did not go, did not telephone, did not use the switchboard, did not go to his team, did not go into the building and did not ask anybody, and has written down that this is a refusal and that it is his and that nobody argued with him about it.** Every route to him is a document and a person who will remember it, and he can be asked one question about anything for ever by anybody, and that is what makes him a door and not a wall, and a door is not a favour. He is not the man of forty-four.
- **THE MAN OF FORTY-EIGHT — third man of the batch, and new to this account as a live debt.** He did the weekly decontamination verification for about eleven weeks in the autumn on his own time with no name against it, and said out loud in a corridor in August 2014 to about four people that a job in November has a department in it and a department is a rota, and it was correct, and he stopped in October, and **he has not been asked about it since and nobody has rung him, and the autumn compliance report is out with a paragraph number on it in front of four hundred and twenty women.**
- **EZRA MBEKI and TREVOR NUNN, 58, a night porter, nineteen years — deliberately not Frances Tolley's sixty-one and twenty-two years, and the two must never be conflated — not on a roster because the roster does not exist.** They read the Saint Orra west handover aloud at ten o'clock at night on Saturday 3 January 2015 in a waiting area with four chairs, in about nine minutes, and went home at about half past six, and **nothing was written down and nothing is going to be and nobody in this borough is going to be told that it worked.**
- **ABU BAKAYOKO, 58.** Twenty-six years at a stand at the top of the lowland market, five in the morning, a bucket, two urns and no drain, a man paid every day to empty the urns twice a day since about 1989 whose name he does not know and has never asked, and a bowser at four pounds a bucket since 28 November with a man on it paid on Fridays out of his own pocket. **He asked to be counted on 13 January 2015 in a room in daylight, and wanted a line in a minute saying that a thing exists at a place where a thing is needed, and gave the state of five of the six in about two minutes, and refused the sixth out loud before anybody asked him and asked for the refusal to be written down. Nobody asked him where the sixth is and nobody is entitled to. His water, his four pounds a bucket and his Tuesday are exactly where they were.**
- **M. FURNEAUX, 61, resident, the rear block, Carrow Lane.** Wrote the most sensible and most dangerous letter anybody has put in front of a records counter in a year, asked for a reason and not a name, was refused in eleven seconds, sent his letter back with nothing in it, and has not written again and will in about four years.
- **DOREEN WHITLOCK, about sixty, eleven years.** Reads every answer in the housing office book aloud and is a column on it, and put a cup of tea down at the end of a table for a man who did not ask for one, and told a man of fifty-six in a corridor on 1 December that a person who is findable is a person somebody can ask, and she was not talking to him, and Jonas Mercer was not in the corridor.
- **ALDEN ROOK, 46, CivicCore operations director.** **Unsoftened and right and not in a room in this batch. His cover note's sentence is now in two files in two buildings, and a chief officer put it in a borough record on purpose, and in about four years somebody is going to come with a piece of paper and find out which building it is in.** The audit is still public and still the best thing in the borough.
- **PRUE CALLOWAY, 58, borough safety panel chair, eleven years.** **Her finding of 23 April was stated out loud, once, in a room, in daylight, on 28 January 2015, and is not resolved, and it may not be opened a second time in this volume.** She was not in the room and does not know it was said.
- **CYNTHIA AKINTOLA, 61. IVY MARSDEN, 72. STANLEY UMEH, 58. KATHLEEN FERRIS, 33. BERNICE OFORI, 34. Margo Doré. Sanaa Iqbal. Ivo Bamba. Yvonne Amoah. Gloria Nye. Winifred Crabbe. Ines Tarrant. Jonas Mercer.** All present, all unchanged in their standing positions, **and none of them was helped in this batch and none of them was rescued and none of them was thanked for anything.**
- **BEA OSUNDE, the woman of about sixty at the barrier end, NORA BELL, crossing guard, nineteen years, and the woman of thirty-four at the bottom of Quarry Street** are three different people and their numbers are three different things, and **nine hundred and forty is a number of times, nine hundred and eighty-six is a number of Wednesdays, and fourteen is a difference between two public numbers, and none of the three is a number of people and none of them has ever been in one sentence with another and none of them may be.**

# VOLUME 03, BATCH 0003 — CHARACTER STATE AFTER CHAPTER 130

**Nobody in Chapters 121–130 was helped, nobody was rescued, nobody was thanked for anything, nobody refused to be thanked, and no person was asked to do anything they had not already decided to do.**

- **JONAS MERCER, 32.** Stage 2, a rule mender, a transfer steward in practice and not in title. On the register of attachment as LAST WORKING SYSTEM ADMINISTRATOR, CITY OF NACRE — civic standing, no grade, no department, no probation, not subject to review, **released by no person.** Not a party, not a member, not a departmental officer, and he may not become one. He is in a gallery, in a corridor, or he is not in the room. **HE ASKED AT MOST ONE QUESTION IN ANY PUBLIC ROOM IN EVERY CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH AND IN TWO CHAPTERS HE ASKED NONE AT ALL (0122, 0123, 0124, 0125, 0130).** In this batch he said, out loud, in a room in daylight, the answer to what a service floor costs, and it is now in a public minute with no names in it: **a service floor costs the people who are on it and not the people who use it; the price is findability.** He is two men findable because of things he said in rooms, and a third thing he did not start, and he cannot unmake any of them, and he did not make a fourth. **He has now refused five times to stand in that corridor, out loud, in words, to a porter, and the fourth of those refusals was the one he did not make.** His pad carries a reason about a receipt, a reason about a handle, a reason about a hand in front of a face, a reason about a number of nine, and a reason about a fifth time being a duty. **He asked one question in nine months of arguing that he is not going to be able to take back, and it was five words at a counter, and it was about a correction, and the answer was that a correction is not a document, not a return, not a minute and not a file, and if it could be made to go nowhere it would be worthless, and if it could be made to go somewhere it would be a record, and those are the same door and it only opens into a file.** He is not going to Gantry Ward. He is not going to look for the hand that puts the strip in the drawer. He is not going to look for the man of thirty-eight. He has stopped keeping a list of the times a person has been put in front of him.
- **NINA CALDER, about fifty, nineteen years in that office and designing lists since 1999 and the two numbers are not the same number.** She is the only person who comes down to that counter from the second floor, at about ten and at about three, because nobody has ever told her to and nobody could. **She is NOT the woman of about fifty who has been at the second-floor counter for eleven years; they are two different people, they are the same age, they work on the same floor, and neither has ever confused the other in public.** Seven refusals in nineteen years, and she has now refused the same request a second time from a second man and did NOT make it an eighth, and she says the words out loud in a room in daylight: **IT IS NOT A LIST.** She has nine slips in a drawer under a counter with no key and no list of what is in it, and she keeps a copy of every one she has written, **which is not a copy of a document, because there is no document and there never was one, and a drawer of them is not a file and cannot be produced by anybody**, and she has not been asked how many and is not going to tell, and the back of her hand is not a book. **Nine slips is a count of documents and about eleven people a day is a count of people and the two are not the same number and must never be added together, and she has given neither figure to anybody, and the count of nine is the count of the account and not the count of a person. She has said out loud that a piece of paper only gets written when a person stands in front of her and asks what was true on a day, and that it is remarkable and a little frightening how few of them do.** **She has refused, out loud and unasked, to say which of the two conditions on the wall is operative, and would rather stand under a contradiction for another four years than be the woman who settled it. She has read a letter in a tray on the second floor and has not opened it in front of a second person and has not answered it in twenty-three days as at 13 March 2015 and has told nobody it is there. She is about to be proved right about the second half of her own sentence — a register that grows when nobody is hurt is a register somebody can hold over you — and it will not be about the bulb, and Jonas Mercer has worked out that he is not going to be in the room and has not told her.** She gave the batch its only thing that was both free and a use, to a stranger, for nothing, in about eleven seconds: the counter works because a person is on it, and she is not findable, and if she stopped coming down there would be a counter and there would not be a counter. **In that answer she described the drawer and said nothing whatever about how many were in it, which is correct, and the batch's hardest rule held.**
- **BEATRICE OSUNDE, about sixty, at the barrier end of that street for something like thirty-one years, oiling a bench.** **THE SENTENCE OF BATCH 0003 IS HERS AND IT IS THE ONE SHE SAID ONCE AND DID NOT SAY TWICE: YOU HAVE BEEN FINDING PEOPLE FOR EIGHT MONTHS AND YOU HAVE NOT YET FOUND OUT THAT THE EXPENSIVE HALF IS NOT BEING FOUND. IT IS BEING ASKED.** She also gave him the receipt: a man who can be asked one question about anything, for ever, by anybody, is not findable, he is available, and a handle is cheap, and a receipt is not an apology, and the whole of what he has been protecting that man from for eight months is a bill. **She did not argue, did not improve it, and did not tell him he was brave, which she has refused to do since the fourth of September and has been right about four times.** The twelve words are hers and are unchanged: *being findable is not the same as being useful.*
- **BRAM OSEI, porter, Saint Orra west, the day bearer.** His Thursday is still refused on the board in his own handwriting with *no reason I can give* under a *no reason given* in somebody else's hand, and he has asked twice that the second line not be looked at, and nobody has looked at it. **In this batch he said the batch's most exact refusal back to itself — the only instrument in this borough that keeps a man from being askable is a man who does not know, and there is no other one, and that is also true about me — and he accepted, on purpose, being made a person who knows something, and said he does not want to be two, and he has told nobody that Jonas Mercer is not going to be in that room on 7 March.** He is not on a rota, not on a board, not in any instrument in this city, and he is the reason a man of forty-eight has not been asked.
- **ABU BAKAYOKO, 58.** Twenty-six years at a stand at the top of the lowland market, five in the morning, a bucket, two urns and no drain, and a man he pays to empty them twice a day and has never once asked the name of. **He came back twice in this batch, on 2 February and 13 February, and he is right to and the batch may not make him un-right.** He has three pieces of paper in an inside pocket and a copy of the minute of 15 January and a bowser and a man on the bowser paid on Fridays out of his own pocket. **He has worked out, standing at a counter, in about nine seconds, that a man who can be wrong in public is not a man who has to be right in a van.** His refusal of the sixth water point stands, is minuted, and nobody may ask him where it is. The sixth shape will not be named in this volume in any document that leaves the street. **He did not get his Tuesday back and nobody is.**
- **EMMANUEL OTIENO, 38.** Agency, ten years, four agencies in nine years and the same two in the last four. Nights at a depot, four to ten, and a second job on Fridays he does not talk about. Rents the top floor of a building on a road he has never seen the name of on any paper. **A daughter of nine who walks to a bus stop at the end of that road.** He is not on any list, not a member of anything, no claim, no reference, no party, nothing in any file in this city. **He has been to a counter five times in his life and four of them were in that vestibule in the first week of February. He has a plastic wallet in the glovebox of a van he does not own with more than one piece of paper in it, and nobody in this city can say how many, and he has shown it to nobody. He has worked out, alone, in a kitchen, on a Sunday, that a date can be wrong and that if it is wrong you can come back, and then that he can now do this to anything, and he stood at a sink and felt something he did not have a word for and the word he did not have a word for was powerful, and it is not power and he does not know that.** He was refused a state about a bus stop in about eleven seconds and was not angry and said eleven words on the way out. He was not helped and was not rescued and nobody gave him anything.
- **HOWARD BRAMBLE, 61.** Fourth floor of a block of forty flats in Tideglass, on the estate with the parade of shops on the top. Nineteen months. A wife who cannot carry anything heavier than a kettle. He went and asked for the unsigned extract himself in the third week of January. He asked for a reason column in person on 16 February, was refused in the right order in about eleven seconds, said the refusal was right, and said that in about four years there is going to be nothing at all to put on the table for a frightened person in a kitchen. **HE IS NOT M. FURNEAUX AND MUST NEVER BE CONFUSED WITH HIM.** M. Furneaux is 61, resident, the rear block, Carrow Lane, wrote once on 2 January, was refused, and is not going to write again before about 2018. **The coincidence of their age is a coincidence and nobody in this borough is to be allowed to make it a pattern.**
- **THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY WHO ASKED FOR A STATE ABOUT A PERSON, Friday 6 March 2015.** Not named, not on any list. His sister went out on 9 February with a bag of clothes. He was refused in about eleven seconds and correctly, asked why she does this at all, was answered about a drawer, said that was the answer to his question and he had not asked it, and went out into the rain with nothing at all. **His sister is not Bernice Ofori and nothing in that scene refers to her.**
- **PETER NAYLOR, 44.** Level-three acceptance officer, field services, Gantry Ward, out of estates since 2011. **A wall.** Signed an acceptance in about ninety seconds in August without knowing what any of the words mean; was read two sentences in a corridor in January and was able to say no and did not and does not know he was in it. **NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH IS ABLE TO ASK HIM ONE QUESTION ABOUT ANY OF IT, EVER.** He has a fortnight somewhere in this city with a bucket and a tap; one came round at the end of February, in four degrees, with a frost warning out for the twenty-eighth. **Nobody helped him. Nobody asked him. Nobody is going to be able to ask him whether he has got a coat. Unresolved.**
- **ROYDEN ACHEBE, 49.** NDC field services manager. A door, which is not a favour. **STILL NOT TOLD, BY NOBODY, IN FEBRUARY OR AT ANY POINT IN THIS BATCH, and Jonas Mercer has now said out loud in a corridor that he is not going to go, with the reason on the back page of a pad.** He can be asked one question about anything, for ever, by anybody, and he is not untouchable, and there is no argument in this borough in which not asking him is the right thing to do, and he is not going to be asked. He was not consulted, not telephoned, not visited, and does not know. **The two must never be conflated in prose, in a document or in a narration.**
- **THE MAN OF FORTY-EIGHT.** Not a wall and not a door. Said a correct thing in a corridor in August about a job in November having a department in it, did a weekly verification for about eleven weeks in the autumn on his own time with no name against it, stopped in October. **HAS NOT BEEN ASKED, HAS NOT BEEN RUNG, AND JONAS MERCER HAS NOW REFUSED OUT LOUD IN A CORRIDOR TO GO AND FIND HIM, and Bram Osei agreed with the reason. He is safer not knowing. Unresolved and the compliance paragraph is unanswered.**
- **SANA A IQBAL — DR SANAA IQBAL.** Twenty minutes a week, refused in her own words in May, on the log since 9 May, and behind paragraph 4.11 with four hundred and twenty women. **NOT ASKED IN THIS BATCH AND NOT GOING TO BE.** Her refusal stands, unargued, and the machine in that room is still running.
